# Campaign c1 — start here (wrap-up snapshot, 2026-11-09)
Goal (user, latest): methodology + tools for fitting a very large MoE (~500 GB weights -> 128 GB unified memory + 4 TB SSD) at similar accuracy and acceptable tokens/s. Proxy: ibm-granite/granite-3.1-1b-a400m-instruct on llama.cpp (commit 31288c9c6), RTX 5070 Ti (discrete). Every result is labelled transferable / discrete-only / prediction (D012).

## What is here
- `decisions/D001..D020` — chronological decisions with evidence (read D012-D020 first).
- `LAB-FEASIBILITY.md`, `MANAGER-DESIGN.md`, `cc-inventory.csv` — Lab Manager findings and the CC inventory (observed vs inferred).
- `bin/` — `run_op` (recorded commands), `lab` (image/job/attempt/cancel/reconcile/register/image-load/chaos), `perf_summary`, `index_evidence`, `cost_report`, `cuda_compile_check`.
- `cc/` — Build CC (`build_engine`), `engine_handoff`, `routing_trace` (patch + replay), `memory_pareto`, `hybrid_expert` (Opus harness), `q8_reuse` (UNTESTED speed patch), `gpu_budget` (memory-restriction shim, may be incomplete), tests (`pytest` in each dir).
- `evidence/*.jsonl` — raw per-agent streams (intent/started/outcome); `index/ops.jsonl` merged; `lab/jobs/*` job/attempt state + results; `experiments/` summaries; `claims/paper-claims.md` (15 source-supported claims, none tested yet).
Not committed (reproducible/bulky): llama.cpp clone (`ref/`), image archives, nsys/ncu reports, base logits, traces (regenerate with the lab tests), Codex scratch trees. Models live in `~/models/campaign` (Granite pin 0da7a48b; GGUFs bf16/Q8_0/Q4_K_M/mixE4K/3K/2K).

## Findings to trust (with caveats in the D-notes)
1. Experts are 90.4% of weight bytes; mixed precision (experts Q4_K, rest Q8_0) halves Q4_K_M's quality loss at equal memory (D013).
2. Static layer offload (`--n-cpu-moe`) cuts GPU MiB linearly but decode collapses (discrete-only, D014). Page-cache-as-expert-cache has a sharp cliff when RAM < working set (D015, contaminated by concurrent compiles).
3. Granite routing skew is real vs a uniform control (D017), mild, weaker pooled across workloads.
4. Hybrid hit/miss dispatch is bitwise-exact; the serial cost model holds (33 us/miss); perfect-overlap upper bound NOT supported (D019).
5. Engine-native `--moe-cache-mib` (LRU, upload-on-miss) is slower than no cache until ~60% coverage (job-d50c052f94). The matched static-offload comparison in the same tool did not finish (D020) — rerun `lab/tests/static1.json`.
6. Build CC: failures recorded (3 failed attempts), ccache makes patched rebuilds ~10-20 s; image identity bug found by independent observation (D016); real handoff `accepted` for the corrected record (experiments in `cc/engine_handoff/example-real5`).
7. Lab core bugs found by testing recovery per phase (D006, D020); duplicate delivery, sandbox kill, retry-as-new-attempt, stale/conflicting result rejection all demonstrated (LAB-FEASIBILITY.md, MANAGER-DESIGN.md).

## Unfinished (honest list)
Hard GPU-memory restriction shim (T-L) not compiled/tested by me; Strata concepts not yet applied end-to-end (only studied + CPU tests, and the single-layer harness); static hot-set expert placement (managed-memory idea, D018) not started; no end-to-end speed/memory result beats the baselines in a way I would call an engine win; q8_reuse patch not compiled; Opus/Codex outputs only partly reviewed; Claude-side token cost not captured.

## Host state to restore (I changed these with your approval, D002)
Stopped: container `euaaa-llm-gpu-1` (`docker start euaaa-llm-gpu-1`) and user unit Sunshine (`systemctl --user start app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`). GPU lock removed (D007). No host-wide driver/profiling change was made. Campaign containers are labelled `campaign=c1` (none should be running).

`pip`-free: python3 stdlib + PyYAML/pytest. Re-create the lab: `bin/lab image add llamacpp-31288c9 ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp@sha256:395d01bb47eb23d5e967129c6ebd2b5969365401621e16dd3db33e50fa7462e3`; build an engine: `python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py --source <llama.cpp> --commit 31288c9c6 [--patch P] [--extra-target T] --tag X --out builds/results/Y` (needs BASE_RUNTIME digest, see cc/build_engine/README.md).

- `cc/resource_observe/`: backends `tegrastats`, `/proc` + cgroup v2, `nvml` (x86). # build_engine

Use this capability to turn a clean, identified local llama.cpp checkout and an optional Git patch into a local, runtime-only CUDA image and an evidence directory. It targets linux/amd64 and CUDA architecture 120 (RTX 5070 Ti). Model weights are supplied separately at runtime.

Requires Python 3.12+ (stdlib only), Git, Docker daemon access, and Docker Buildx/Bake. pytest is needed only for tests. No GPU is needed to compile or collect hashes. The builder installs Ubuntu build packages with apt; an actual build needs cached packages/base layers or repository/registry access. This implementation does not download source, patches, models, or web UI assets. The existing `campaign/cuda-tools:c1` image is not used as the builder because the required builder base is the digest-pinned NVIDIA devel image.

## Run

Run from the campaign directory. Give every attempt a new or empty output directory. While executing assignment T-D, keep outputs under `cc/build_engine/` or `builds/llamacpp/`.

```bash
# Supply the real runtime image digest from trusted/local image evidence.
export BASE_RUNTIME='nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04@sha256:<64-hex-digest>'
python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py \
  --source ref/llama.cpp --commit 31288c9c6 \
  --tag campaign/llamacpp:c1 --out cc/build_engine/results/baseline
```

The placeholder must be replaced; it is not a working digest. If BASE_RUNTIME is unset, the CLI inspects the local runtime tag and selects its NVIDIA RepoDigest without pulling it. Missing local images or RepoDigests fail at `base_images`. BASE_DEVEL defaults to the devel digest already recorded in `artifacts/op-309e1f95c716/stdout`; override it with a full `nvidia/cuda:12.8.1-devel-ubuntu24.04@sha256:...` reference when needed. Both bases are validated and supplied as separate name and digest Dockerfile arguments. The CLI never builds from a floating base tag.

To add a patch, save a unified Git diff to a file and add `--patch path/to/change.patch`. Source HEAD must resolve to `--commit`; tracked changes and untracked files cause rejection. The source checkout remains read-only: Git optional locks are disabled, a `git archive` snapshot is extracted under the output directory, and `git apply --check` runs there before `git apply`. Git discovery stops before the enclosing campaign repository. Binary patches supported by Git are accepted. Submodules are rejected. Git archive honors committed export attributes; ignored and untracked files and `.git` are omitted. Docker ignore files in the staged snapshot are emptied to prevent omission of tracked source. Temporary staging is removed after either result. Keep the supplied patch and original commit for rebuilding; patch bytes are identified by SHA256 but are not retained as a separate output artifact.

The image contains only the seven requested tools in `/app`, their generated shared libraries and the OpenMP runtime, on top of the CUDA runtime base. It has no compiler, source checkout, or weights. Its entrypoint is cleared, so invoke tools by full path, for example `/app/llama-bench`. Release/shared CUDA compilation uses the flags in `build-record.json`; CPU-native tuning, tests, downloaded UI, and OpenSSL are disabled. `LLAMA_CURL=OFF` is passed as requested, although this checkout treats LLAMA_CURL as deprecated. Source and patch identity are recorded as image labels; binaries' built-in Git version may say `unknown` because `.git` is not staged.

## Outputs and failure handling

`build-record.json` uses schema version 1. It records status, failure stage/error, requested and resolved commit, Git tree ID and dirty status, patch SHA256 or null, tag/platform, recipe SHA256 and sizes, base references/digests, Docker and Buildx versions, CMake flags, Buildx metadata, image config ID/RepoDigests/Created/Architecture/Os, tool SHA256 values, saved archive SHA256/bytes, build duration and total duration. Fields remain null or empty when a failure occurs before collection. `build_wall_seconds` measures the Bake invocation, including export; `wall_seconds` covers the whole attempt.

The other files are:

- `build.stdout` and `build.stderr`: full subprocess stdout/stderr, including compiler output and diagnostics on failure. Binary Git archive output is directed to staging rather than the logs.
- `buildx-metadata.json`: Buildx metadata, when the build produces it; retained even when the build exits nonzero.
- `engine-image.docker.tar`: `docker save` of the built immutable image config ID, on success. Its bytes and SHA256 are recorded after saving.

The CLI exits 0 only after all evidence collection succeeds, otherwise nonzero. Failures include source mismatch/dirty tree, unsupported submodules, malformed or inapplicable patch, unavailable Docker/base image, build/export failure, incorrect architecture, missing binaries, save failure, or malformed archive. A failure after building can leave the tagged local image and partial evidence; inspect `failure_stage` and retry in a fresh output directory. Invalid CLI arguments, an unwritable output path, or a nonempty output directory fail before a record can be created. Existing evidence is never overwritten. The CLI does not push, prune, mount the Docker socket in an image, or operate on unrelated containers. A single short-lived `docker run --rm --network=none --read-only --entrypoint /usr/bin/sha256sum` container hashes the tools without requesting a GPU. Subsequent hashing and saving use the immutable config ID so a later tag change cannot change the evidence target.

Bake requests maximum provenance and saves metadata separately. This does not imply provenance survives image loading and `docker save`. The archive inspector checks `index.json` and reachable OCI manifests for actual in-toto SLSA provenance statements. A classic Docker archive without an OCI index records `retained: false`; an SBOM or an attestation annotation alone does not count. A save or inspection failure leaves provenance unconfirmed. No signature or attestation trust verification is performed.

## Validation without a build

From `builds/llamacpp/`, run `docker buildx bake --print`; the retained `bake-print.json` is the validated default expansion. Its runtime digest is intentionally empty until supplied; print mode validates Bake syntax, not base availability or compilation. For a direct Bake build, supply digest-pinned BASE_DEVEL and BASE_RUNTIME plus SOURCE_DIR, SOURCE_COMMIT and PATCH_SHA256, and use a prepared staging snapshot. Prefer the CLI, which verifies those inputs. Bake uses `BAKE_CMD_CONTEXT` to locate the recipe Dockerfile outside the source context; invoke it from the recipe directory.

From the campaign directory, run:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q \
  cc/build_engine/test_build_engine.py \
  --basetemp=cc/build_engine/.pytest-tmp \
  -o cache_dir=cc/build_engine/.pytest_cache
```

# Assignment J-T2 — portable resource-observation CC (host jetson-arm; parent campaign c1; owner Opus-jetson; worker Codex)

Base: branch `jetson/c1` (from f0e676b). Python 3.10 stdlib only (+ pytest for tests). Write ONLY under `campaign/cc/resource_observe/`. Do not touch other campaign files, nvpmodel/clocks, drivers, or install anything.

## Question / output
A small library + CLI `resource_observe.py` that samples resource state on either host and emits JSONL records under ONE common contract with explicit platform backends.

Backends (auto-detected, each can be unavailable with a reason):
- `tegrastats` (Jetson): spawn `tegrastats --interval <ms>` and parse lines. Fixture: `fixtures/tegrastats-idle-orin-nano-r36.5.txt`. Fields: RAM used/total MB (SHARED CPU+GPU DRAM — attribution scope `system-shared-dram`), lfb, SWAP used/total/cached, per-CPU load%@MHz, GR3D_FREQ % (and @MHz if present), EMC_FREQ if present, temperatures (named), power rails (instant/avg mW, rail names vary by board — parse generically).
- `proc` (both): /proc/meminfo (MemTotal, MemAvailable, Cached, SwapTotal/Free, plus NvMap* if present), /proc/loadavg, optional per-PID RSS/VmHWM from /proc/<pid>/status (attribution `process`), cgroup v2 memory.current/memory.peak/memory.max for a given cgroup path (attribution `cgroup`; note cgroup does NOT necessarily account nvmap/driver GPU allocations on Tegra — mark `accounting_note`).
- `sysfs_tegra` (Jetson): GPU devfreq cur/min/max freq (`/sys/devices/platform/17000000.gpu/devfreq/17000000.gpu/`), thermal zones (`/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/{type,temp}`), nvpmodel mode string passed in or read via `nvpmodel -q` (query only).
- `nvml` (x86): `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,temperature.gpu,power.draw --format=csv,noheader,nounits` and per-process `--query-compute-apps`. Attribution `device-discrete`. On Orin this must report unavailable (nvidia-smi absent or no memory fields) — never mandatory.

## Contract (each sample record)
`{"schema":"resource-observe/0","ts":ISO8601 UTC,"mono_s":float,"host_id":str,"backend":str,"seq":int,"metrics":[{"name","value","unit","scope","source"}...],"unavailable":[{"name","backend","reason"}],"parse_errors":[...]}`
Rules: no false zeros (missing → `unavailable` with reason); units explicit (MiB, MHz, percent, mW, celsius); never sum tegrastats RAM with process RSS or cgroup (different scopes of the same physical pages); a malformed line yields a record with `parse_errors` and the raw line hash, not a crash.
CLI: `resource_observe.py sample --backends auto|tegrastats,proc,... [--interval-ms 500] [--duration-s N] [--pid P] [--cgroup PATH] --out FILE.jsonl` and `resource_observe.py summarize FILE.jsonl` (per-metric min/max/mean/high-water + coverage: expected vs received samples, gaps > 2x interval).
Also `capabilities` subcommand: prints which backends/metrics are available on this host with reasons.

## Tests (`test_resource_observe.py`, pytest, no GPU, no root)
Parse the real fixture; malformed tegrastats lines (truncated, missing RAM, unknown rail names, extra fields, empty); missing /proc fields via fixture files; nvml CSV fixture incl. `[N/A]` values; summarize coverage gap detection; no-double-count assertion. Allow injecting fixture roots/paths so tests don't depend on the host.

## Limits / checkpoint
Time 30 min. Run the tests and ONE real 3-second `sample --backends auto` on this host (it is a Jetson Orin Nano) writing to `cc/resource_observe/fixtures/live-sample.jsonl`. Add `README.md` (agent-facing: usage, contract, per-backend attribution limits). Final message: files, test result line, live capability output, known gaps.

Rules: no false zeros (missing → `unavailable` with reason); units explicit (MiB, MHz, percent, mW, celsius); never sum tegrastats RAM with process RSS or cgroup (different scopes of the same physical pages); a malformed line yields a record with `parse_errors` and the raw line hash, not a crash.
CLI: `resource_observe.py sample --backends auto|tegrastats,proc,... [--interval-ms 500] [--duration-s N] [--pid P] [--cgroup PATH] --out FILE.jsonl` and `resource_observe.py summarize FILE.jsonl` (per-metric min/max/mean/high-water + coverage: expected vs received samples, gaps > 2x interval).
Also `capabilities` subcommand: prints which backends/metrics are available on this host with reasons.

## Tests (`test_resource_observe.py`, pytest, no GPU, no root)
Parse the real fixture; malformed tegrastats lines (truncated, missing RAM, unknown rail names, extra fields, empty); missing /proc fields via fixture files; nvml CSV fixture incl. `[N/A]` values; summarize coverage gap detection; no-double-count assertion. Allow injecting fixture roots/paths so tests don't depend on the host.

## Limits / checkpoint
Time 30 min. Run the tests and ONE real 3-second `sample --backends auto` on this host (it is a Jetson Orin Nano) writing to `cc/resource_observe/fixtures/live-sample.jsonl`. Add `README.md` (agent-facing: usage, contract, per-backend attribution limits). Final message: files, test result line, live capability output, known gaps.

# Assignment J-T2 — portable resource-observation CC (host jetson-arm; parent campaign c1; owner Opus-jetson; worker Codex)

Base: branch `jetson/c1` (from f0e676b). Python 3.10 stdlib only (+ pytest for tests). Write ONLY under `campaign/cc/resource_observe/`. Do not touch other campaign files, nvpmodel/clocks, drivers, or install anything.

## Question / output
A small library + CLI `resource_observe.py` that samples resource state on either host and emits JSONL records under ONE common contract with explicit platform backends.

Backends (auto-detected, each can be unavailable with a reason):
- `tegrastats` (Jetson): spawn `tegrastats --interval <ms>` and parse lines. Fixture: `fixtures/tegrastats-idle-orin-nano-r36.5.txt`. Fields: RAM used/total MB (SHARED CPU+GPU DRAM — attribution scope `system-shared-dram`), lfb, SWAP used/total/cached, per-CPU load%@MHz, GR3D_FREQ % (and @MHz if present), EMC_FREQ if present, temperatures (named), power rails (instant/avg mW, rail names vary by board — parse generically).
- `proc` (both): /proc/meminfo (MemTotal, MemAvailable, Cached, SwapTotal/Free, plus NvMap* if present), /proc/loadavg, optional per-PID RSS/VmHWM from /proc/<pid>/status (attribution `process`), cgroup v2 memory.current/memory.peak/memory.max for a given cgroup path (attribution `cgroup`; note cgroup does NOT necessarily account nvmap/driver GPU allocations on Tegra — mark `accounting_note`).
- `sysfs_tegra` (Jetson): GPU devfreq cur/min/max freq (`/sys/devices/platform/17000000.gpu/devfreq/17000000.gpu/`), thermal zones (`/sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/{type,temp}`), nvpmodel mode string passed in or read via `nvpmodel -q` (query only).
- `nvml` (x86): `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total,utilization.gpu,clocks.sm,temperature.gpu,power.draw --format=csv,noheader,nounits` and per-process `--query-compute-apps`. Attribution `device-discrete`. On Orin this must report unavailable (nvidia-smi absent or no memory fields) — never mandatory.

## Contract (each sample record)
`{"schema":"resource-observe/0","ts":ISO8601 UTC,"mono_s":float,"host_id":str,"backend":str,"seq":int,"metrics":[{"name","value","unit","scope","source"}...],"unavailable":[{"name","backend","reason"}],"parse_errors":[...]}`
Rules: no false zeros (missing → `unavailable` with reason); units explicit (MiB, MHz, percent, mW, celsius); never sum tegrastats RAM with process RSS or cgroup (different scopes of the same physical pages); a malformed line yields a record with `parse_errors` and the raw line hash, not a crash.
CLI: `resource_observe.py sample --backends auto|tegrastats,proc,... [--interval-ms 500] [--duration-s N] [--pid P] [--cgroup PATH] --out FILE.jsonl` and `resource_observe.py summarize FILE.jsonl` (per-metric min/max/mean/high-water + coverage: expected vs received samples, gaps > 2x interval).
Also `capabilities` subcommand: prints which backends/metrics are available on this host with reasons.

## Tests (`test_resource_observe.py`, pytest, no GPU, no root)
Parse the real fixture; malformed tegrastats lines (truncated, missing RAM, unknown rail names, extra fields, empty); missing /proc fields via fixture files; nvml CSV fixture incl. `[N/A]` values; summarize coverage gap detection; no-double-count assertion. Allow injecting fixture roots/paths so tests don't depend on the host.

## Limits / checkpoint
Time 30 min. Run the tests and ONE real 3-second `sample --backends auto` on this host (it is a Jetson Orin Nano) writing to `cc/resource_observe/fixtures/live-sample.jsonl`. Add `README.md` (agent-facing: usage, contract, per-backend attribution limits). Final message: files, test result line, live capability output, known gaps.

# D005 — 2-chunk PPL smoke gate calibration (E001, 5 A/A attempts)
- Evidence: experiments/E001-ppl-baseline/attempts/a1..a5/{result.json,stdout.txt}; ops in evidence/orchestrator.jsonl.
- Observed: PPL = 7.5325 in all 5 attempts (spread 0.0000%), each ~2.8 s wall, all owned containers removed, GPU lock uncontended.
- Reported statistical error of the metric itself: +/- 0.84642 (~11%) over 2 chunks.
- Interpretation: the gate is a DETERMINISM/regression tripwire for same-weights, same-precision, same-kernels candidates (a 1% relative change is ~100x the observed run noise but ~1/11 of the metric's own sampling error). It cannot establish equivalence of a candidate that changes numerics or routing; those need paired token-level comparison (logit/top-k/KL) and routing-ID equality.
- Frozen policy (provisional): candidate passes smoke if |PPL_c - 7.5325| / 7.5325 <= 1% AND same engine/weights/precision; any other change class must add the targeted check from the test catalog.
- Limit: determinism measured on one GPU state/driver/container; not across GPU clocks, other hardware, or thread counts (CPU-offload variants may differ).
- Would change: nondeterminism appearing under CPU offload or multi-sequence batching -> re-calibrate with A/A for each configuration.

# Assignment J-T4 — lab: per-host capability profiles, platform admission, portable GPU request/telemetry (host jetson-arm; parent c1; owner Opus-jetson; worker Codex)

Base: branch `jetson/c1`. File: `bin/lab` (275 lines, x86-written; Python 3.10 here). Read `MANAGER-DESIGN.md` §admission if present, `decisions/D022-*.md`, `cc/resource_observe/README.md`.
Allowed files: `bin/lab`, new `lab/hosts/*.json`, new `lab/test_lab_hosts.py`. Do NOT change existing job/attempt state semantics, result fields, or `lab/jobs/*` history (x86 evidence). x86 behaviour must be byte-for-byte the same command lines when the host profile is `x86-main` (default when no host profile is configured).

## Observed x86-only assumptions to remove (verified by Opus)
1. `--gpus all` → on Jetson the GPU request is `--runtime nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility` (D022).
2. `nvidia-smi memory.used` polling: on Orin nvidia-smi exists but prints `[N/A]` → `int()` crashes the runner mid-attempt. Make the GPU sampler a host-profile choice: `nvml` (x86, unchanged) or `tegrastats` (Jetson: shared DRAM RAM used MB via `cc/resource_observe/resource_observe.py` parser functions imported or a `tegrastats --interval 250` child; record scope `system-shared-dram`, never label it GPU memory). Unparseable values → field null + reason, never crash, never 0.
3. `gpu_state()` likewise (check what it calls) → backend-aware with `unavailable` reasons.
4. docker invocation: add env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX` support (this session needs `sg docker -c` with a single quoted command string — implement by shlex-joining argv when the prefix is set).

## Host profile + admission (new)
- `lab/hosts/<host_id>.json`: `{host_id, platform: "linux/arm64"|"linux/amd64", gpu: {request: "gpus-all"|"nvidia-runtime-env", sampler: "nvml"|"tegrastats", memory_domain: "discrete-vram"|"shared-dram", arch: "sm_87"|"sm_120"}, l4t_major (Jetson only), resources_max: {cpus, memory}, capabilities: [..]}`. Host id comes from `~/.config/siminfeng/host_id` (as in `bin/run_op` evdir), default `x86-main`. Write `lab/hosts/jetson-arm.json` (6 CPUs, memory max 5g for test containers, l4t_major 36, sm_87) and `lab/hosts/x86-main.json` (8 cpus/16g, sm_120, matching current defaults).
- Image records (`lab/images/*.json`) may carry `platform` and `target_requirements` (Build CC schema 2: platform, l4t_major, cuda_arch, runtime). `lab image add` gains optional `--platform` and `--requirements <build-record.json>`.
- `lab submit` performs admission against the current host and records a decision file `admission.json` in the job dir with `decision: accepted|rejected|needs_information`, `reasons[]`, host profile sha256: reject on platform mismatch, cuda_arch mismatch, l4t_major mismatch, resources above host max; `needs_information` when the image record lacks platform/requirements or the model/data path is missing. Rejected/needs_information jobs are still written (job.json + admission.json, read-only) and `lab run` refuses them (exit code 10 with reason). Legacy images with no platform on x86-main stay accepted with reason "legacy image record: platform unverified" (do not break x86).
- `lab status` shows admission decision.

## Tests (`lab/test_lab_hosts.py`, pytest, no docker/GPU): profile loading/default, argv generation for both GPU request modes (+ DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX quoting), tegrastats/nvml sampler parse incl. `[N/A]` → null, admission accept/reject/needs_information matrix, x86 argv unchanged vs a golden list built from the current code. Monkeypatch subprocess. Run with `python3 -m pytest -q lab/test_lab_hosts.py`.

## Limits
Time 45 min. Do not run docker, the GPU, or `lab run`. Final message ≤ 20 lines: files, pytest line, exact commands Opus should use to (a) add the Jetson image from `cc/build_engine/results/jetson-c1/build-record.json`, (b) submit an accepted Jetson job and an amd64 job that must be rejected; open risks.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""gguf_manifest: content identity of a GGUF independent of metadata noise.
Usage: PYTHONPATH=<llama.cpp>/gguf-py python3 gguf_manifest.py MODEL.gguf > manifest.json
Output: file sha256/bytes, tensor_data_sha256 (over name|type|shape|bytes in file order), per-tensor sha256, metadata key/value digest
(values truncated for arrays). Compare two manifests: same tensor_data_sha256 => identical weights even if file sha differs."""
import sys, json, hashlib
from gguf import GGUFReader
p = sys.argv[1]; r = GGUFReader(p)
fh = hashlib.sha256()
with open(p, "rb") as f:
    for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 22), b""): fh.update(b)
tensors, agg = [], hashlib.sha256()
for t in r.tensors:
    d = bytes(t.data.tobytes()); h = hashlib.sha256(d).hexdigest()
    tensors.append(dict(name=t.name, type=t.tensor_type.name, shape=[int(x) for x in t.shape], bytes=len(d), sha256=h))
    agg.update(f"{t.name}|{t.tensor_type.name}|{list(map(int, t.shape))}|{h}\n".encode())
meta = {}
for k, fld in r.fields.items():
    if k.startswith("GGUF."): continue
    try:
        v = fld.contents()
        if isinstance(v, list): v = dict(len=len(v), sha256=hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(v, default=str).encode()).hexdigest())
    except Exception as e: v = f"<unreadable {e}>"
    meta[k] = v
print(json.dumps(dict(schema="gguf-manifest/0", file=p, file_sha256=fh.hexdigest(), n_tensors=len(tensors),
                      tensor_data_sha256=agg.hexdigest(), metadata=meta, tensors=tensors), indent=1, default=str))
EOF

## Observed x86-only assumptions to remove (verified by Opus)
1. `--gpus all` → on Jetson the GPU request is `--runtime nvidia -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility` (D022).
2. `nvidia-smi memory.used` polling: on Orin nvidia-smi exists but prints `[N/A]` → `int()` crashes the runner mid-attempt. Make the GPU sampler a host-profile choice: `nvml` (x86, unchanged) or `tegrastats` (Jetson: shared DRAM RAM used MB via `cc/resource_observe/resource_observe.py` parser functions imported or a `tegrastats --interval 250` child; record scope `system-shared-dram`, never label it GPU memory). Unparseable values → field null + reason, never crash, never 0.
3. `gpu_state()` likewise (check what it calls) → backend-aware with `unavailable` reasons.
4. docker invocation: add env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX` support (this session needs `sg docker -c` with a single quoted command string — implement by shlex-joining argv when the prefix is set).

## Host profile + admission (new)
- `lab/hosts/<host_id>.json`: `{host_id, platform: "linux/arm64"|"linux/amd64", gpu: {request: "gpus-all"|"nvidia-runtime-env", sampler: "nvml"|"tegrastats", memory_domain: "discrete-vram"|"shared-dram", arch: "sm_87"|"sm_120"}, l4t_major (Jetson only), resources_max: {cpus, memory}, capabilities: [..]}`. Host id comes from `~/.config/siminfeng/host_id` (as in `bin/run_op` evdir), default `x86-main`. Write `lab/hosts/jetson-arm.json` (6 CPUs, memory max 5g for test containers, l4t_major 36, sm_87) and `lab/hosts/x86-main.json` (8 cpus/16g, sm_120, matching current defaults).
- Image records (`lab/images/*.json`) may carry `platform` and `target_requirements` (Build CC schema 2: platform, l4t_major, cuda_arch, runtime). `lab image add` gains optional `--platform` and `--requirements <build-record.json>`.
- `lab submit` performs admission against the current host and records a decision file `admission.json` in the job dir with `decision: accepted|rejected|needs_information`, `reasons[]`, host profile sha256: reject on platform mismatch, cuda_arch mismatch, l4t_major mismatch, resources above host max; `needs_information` when the image record lacks platform/requirements or the model/data path is missing. Rejected/needs_information jobs are still written (job.json + admission.json, read-only) and `lab run` refuses them (exit code 10 with reason). - `lab status` shows admission decision.

Findings, ranked. I ran pytest (45 passed) and read the diff plus the J-T4 spec. I did not run docker or `lab run`.

1. **MEDIUM, new x86 failure path (lines ~278-283 `cmd_run`, ~72-90 `admission`).** `lab run` recomputes admission against the host profile and exits 10 if it is not "accepted". That applies to old x86 jobs that have no `admission.json`.
   - Failure scenario: a job submitted at HEAD with `--res memory=24g` or `cpus=16`, or with a test whose `memory` is above 16g, is now refused at run.
   - Another case is `--res memory=16gb`. Docker accepts that form, but `memory_bytes` rejects it (regex `[bkmg]?`).
   - A job whose model or data file has since moved also gets exit 10. The spec only asked for this at submit.
   - Fix: for jobs with no recorded admission, skip re-evaluation or treat them as legacy. Also accept the `kb/mb/gb` suffixes.
2. **MEDIUM, admission is not hashed or bound to the attempt (lines ~250-252).**
   - `admission.json` is only `chmod 444`. The directory is writable, so it can be unlinked or replaced.
   - Its hash is not in `job.json`, the attempt state or `result.json`, so a result cannot be traced to the decision and profile that allowed it.
   - Deleting it only drops back to the recomputed check, so it is not a real bypass.
   - `job.json` is written before `admission.json`. A crash or exception in `admission()` (for example an invalid `td["memory"]` or a missing `resources` key) leaves a job with no record. A resubmit with the same key returns "duplicate submission" and never writes it, so `status` shows "legacy (unrecorded)".
   - Fix: compute the decision first, then write both files, and put `admission_sha256` in `job.json` or the attempt state.
3. **MEDIUM, Jetson sampler: baseline is always null and `unavailable` is always set (lines ~115, ~300-312).**
   - The baseline `sampler.sample()` runs right after `TegrastatsReader` starts, so the queue is empty. It returns `(None, "no tegrastats sample available")`.
   - `sample_reason` is never cleared. Every Jetson test therefore gets `mem.unavailable` set even when peak samples succeeded, and `shared_dram_baseline_mib` is always null.
   - Fix: wait for the first line before taking the baseline, and clear the reason once a sample succeeds.
4. **MEDIUM, `exclusive_before_after` becomes false on Jetson (line ~346).** `gpu_state` returns `compute_apps=None` there, and `None == []` is False. Result: `exclusive_before_after=false` when the real answer is unknown. It should be null.
5. **LOW, `lab image-load` cannot carry platform or requirements.** `cmd_imageload` calls `cmd_image` without `--platform` or `--requirements`. Any Jetson image delivered through `image-load` is always `needs_information`, so use `image add --requirements`. Re-running `image add` with the same image id also silently overwrites the stored platform and requirements, which weakens the immutability of images.
6. **LOW, x86 `gpu_state` semantics changed (lines ~172-178).** If `power.draw` or `clocks.sm` prints `[Not Supported]`, or `compute-apps` prints `[N/A]`, `gpu_pre` and `gpu_post` now become `gpu=None, compute_apps=None`. HEAD recorded the raw string. A failing nvidia-smi now gives `exclusive_before_after=False`, where HEAD gave True.
7. **LOW, x86 `mem` fields change when no sample succeeds.** If no sample succeeds (a very short container), `mem` now has `gpu_peak_mib=null` and `gpu_delta_mib=null` plus an `unavailable` key. HEAD gave `gpu_peak_mib=0` and a negative delta. This is intended by the spec, but it is a result.json difference.
8. **LOW, `status` output changed on x86.** It now prints an extra `job admission=...` line per job before the attempt lines. Any script that parses `status` output will see it.
9. **LOW, unknown host id.** An unknown `host_id` file, or a missing `lab/hosts` file, raises a bare `FileNotFoundError` traceback from `submit`, `run` and `gpu_state`. x86-main is fine because its profile exists.
10. **LOW, process-group cleanup.** The `tegrastats` child is left running if the lab process is SIGKILLed mid-run. `close()` terminates it only on normal paths.

**x86 regression check.**
- **Docker argv:** the x86 `docker run` argv is identical to HEAD, and `container_argv` keeps the same order. Default cpus and memory resolve to "8" and "16g".
- **nvidia-smi sampling:** commands and the success-path parsing are unchanged.
- **State transitions and `result.json`:** on the success path, state transitions and `result.json` keys and order are unchanged.
- **Where x86 differs:** only items 1 and 4 to 8 above. Item 1 is the only new failure exit.

**DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX.** I found no bypass. `docker_argv` is applied in `sh()` and in the `Popen` for `run`. Every other docker call goes through `sh()`: ps, inspect, kill, rm, load and `image inspect`. That covers `owned_containers`, `cid_cgroup`, reconcile, cancel and `imageload`. `shlex.join` correctly quotes the `{{json .Config.Labels}}` templates. An empty prefix leaves argv unchanged.

**Admission and idempotency.**
- Duplicate submission works because it returns before any admission write, and a different spec under the same key is still rejected.
- Resubmitting under the same key cannot flip a rejected or `needs_information` job. The old decision stays, and `run` requires both the recorded and the current decision to be accepted.
- Exit 10 happens before any attempt directory or state is written.

# D023 — llama.cpp auto-fit context consumes Jetson shared DRAM; pin -c in test policy (2026-11-10, jetson-arm)
- Observation: lab test `gen_smoke` (no -c; 24 tokens) on jetson-c1 picked `n_ctx = 45568` (stderr of lab/jobs/job-4433960e61/att-1). Shared-DRAM high-water 6568 MiB vs 1634 MiB baseline (tegrastats RAM used, scope system-shared-dram) on a 7607 MiB device; earlier gen_smoke 5647 MiB. 
- Cause (source-supported): the fit logic sizes context from device free memory (cudaMemGetInfo / ggml_backend_cuda_get_available_uma_memory — the log prints "final available_memory_kb"); on Tegra this is system-available DRAM, so engine residency competes with OS/controller/agent headroom. On x86 the same default only consumes VRAM.
- Decision: Jetson test policies pin context explicitly. Added `lab/tests/jetson.json` (`gen_smoke_c2k`, `ppl2` unchanged since it already passes -c 512). x86's `lab/tests/quality.json` untouched (changing it would change x86 test identity) — x86 owner to decide whether gen_smoke should pin -c too, since its result also depends on free VRAM.
- Applicability rule for Manager/test CCs: on shared-memory platforms any engine default derived from "free device memory" is a host-memory policy; admission must declare it (memory.domain: shared-dram) and the test policy must fix it. A cudaMemGetInfo-interposing budget (x86 cc/gpu_budget, T-L) is the natural cap here — untested on Jetson.
- Also fixed: J-T4b treated J-T4-era admission records without a hash as "mismatch"; now "recorded-unhashed (pre-J-T4b)" and still re-checked (old rejected job still refused).
EOF

payload.last_assistant_message:
**No correctness defect found.** The one real finding is a precision change (item 2). Everything below is from reading source only, with no builds or runs. Line numbers refer to `ref/llama.cpp/ggml/src/ggml-cuda/`.

**1. Unfused graph is safe (no defect).**
- `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_vec_f` has exactly three callers: `ggml-cuda.cu:4264` (gate+bias/up+bias GLU fusion), `:4307` (plain gate/up GLU fusion) and `:4470` (MUL_MAT/MUL_MAT_ID + bias fusion).
- Fusion only commits when the predicate is true, then sets `fused_node_count` and returns `fused_node_count - 1` (`:4330`). The `continue` and fall-through paths never mark nodes consumed. With `false`, the loop falls to the normal per-node switch and each node runs on its own: MUL_MAT_ID gate, MUL_MAT_ID up, then GLU. Nothing can be skipped.
- Expert order and routing weights are untouched. Both MUL_MAT_IDs read the same `ids`, and the routing-weight MUL sits downstream of the down projection and is outside every fusion window the predicate touches.
- The patch also disables the ID+ADD_ID bias fusion (`:4470`), but only for bf16, batch-one, MMF-eligible cases. The bias then runs as a separate ADD_ID, which is the same math.
- Dense bf16 MUL_MAT is not affected, because the patch requires `is_mul_mat_id`.
- Standalone dispatch matches the patch's eligibility test. `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_id` (`:2057-2080`) only routes non-quantized types to mmvf on AMD. `should_use_mmq` is false for bf16, so a bf16 MUL_MAT_ID goes to `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_f` with the same `should_use_mmf` arguments (`src1->ne[2]`, `mul_mat_id=true`) that the patch uses.

**2. Activation precision (the one real change).**
- Yes, `mmf.cuh:202-212` converts F32 activations to `nv_bfloat162` via `ggml_cuda_cast<T>` before the MMA, then accumulates in fp32. The mmvf path keeps activations as float and multiplies them with bf16 weights in fp32.
- The unfused path therefore rounds gate/up inputs to bf16 (8-bit mantissa). That is the most likely source of the mean KLD of 2.7e-4.
- The down projection already took this MMF path in the base, so this adds the same rounding to two more matmuls per layer.
- PPL 8.0332 to 8.0163 is within noise. It is not evidence of better quality, and the 99.6% top-1 agreement matches a small rounding perturbation.

**3. CUDA graphs (no issue).**
- The flag is a function-local `static const`, so it is read once, thread-safely, and is constant for the life of the process. Every capture therefore makes the same fusion decision. First and later tokens take the same path.
- `ggml_cuda_mul_mat_id_needs_sync` (`:2013-2037`) returns false for MMF-eligible cases. Graphs stay enabled (`:2712-2716`) and no stream-sync fallback is hit.
- Fusion applies only when `dst->ne[2] == 1`, so prefill batches are unaffected in either mode.

**4. Patch 02 (block size 128) is safe but nearly unreachable.**
- Safe: capping `max_block_size` at 128 only narrows the `block_size` loop (`mmvf.cu:445`). Case 128 exists in the switch. Shared memory is sized as `warp_size` floats per buffer (`:451`) and the reduction uses `tid/warp_size` (`:319-332`). The strided `col2 += block_size` loops handle any `ncols`. Only the fp accumulation order changes, so the `ncols <= 1024` guard is not needed for correctness.
- Dead code: it requires `ids && fusion.gate && bf16 && ncols_dst==1`, which is exactly the case patch 01 diverts away from fusion when MMF is eligible. With both flags set, patch 02 only fires when MMF is ineligible. If the measured gain was attributed to 02 in combined runs, check that attribution.
- Cosmetic: the combined diff's hunk is awkward, with a context line reused as the new `if` body. It is semantically fine but worth confirming that `git apply --check` passes.

**5. The +19% decode speed is plausible.**
- No computation is skipped, because the GLU consumes both projection outputs. A skipped matmul would not give 99.6% top-1 agreement and a PPL near base.
- The byte-identical 64-token greedy output is believable with a 2.7e-4 mean KLD.
- The ub=1 perplexity run is a good check of this path, because batch-one is the only case where `ne[2]==1` fires. The gain is consistent with the MMF kernel being faster than the mmvf kernel at block 256 for these shapes.
- To rule out a measurement artefact, I'd check:
  - the same flags on a longer greedy run;
  - the PPL result across ub sizes;
  - that nodes executed per token (via `GGML_CUDA_GRAPH_DEBUG` or nsys) do not drop.

# D025 — Full-engine decode gain on Jetson: route bf16 MoE gate/up (batch 1) to MMF instead of fused MMVF (2026-11-10, jetson-arm)
Claim category: **full-engine code gain (local to jetson-arm, sm_87, bf16 Granite-3.1-1b-a400m, batch-1 decode)**. Not transferred to x86 (untested there).
- Candidate: llama.cpp 31288c9c6 + cc/moe_dispatch_sm87/patches/combined-01-02.patch (sha256 9cd5745b…), env-gated, default = upstream. Image campaign/llamacpp:jetson-c1-j3 (Build CC record cc/build_engine/results/jetson-c1-j3/build-record.json, archive b730a81f…). Same image for all arms → only the env switch differs.
- Mechanism (J-T3 source analysis + independent review): the fused gate/up+GLU pattern asks the MMVF heuristic ("src0 rows ≤ 512" → vector kernel, 256 threads, F32 activations); standalone NVIDIA bf16 MUL_MAT_ID uses MMF (tensor-core MMA). `GGML_CUDA_J_MMF_IDS=1` declines that fusion on cc 870 when MMF is eligible. nsys (J-P002): gate/up per layer-token 385 µs fused MMVF → 2×131 µs MMF (+GLU kernel); kernel count +3120/64 tok (nothing skipped); GPU time −8.8% under tracing.
- Speed (J-E005, counterbalanced base,P1,P2,F,F,P2,P1,base; tg128 r5; steady = samples 2-5): base 50.48/50.20, **P1 60.07/60.05 (+19.3%)**, P2 (128-thread MMVF) 59.56/59.30 (+18.0%), all-fusion-off 57.34/57.33 (+13.9%). Depth 1024: base 48.7/48.6 → P1 57.8/57.8 (+19%). Prefill pp512 unchanged (1105–1149 both arms, base inert = same as unpatched image 50.4).
- Quality: batch-512 ppl20 identical (path not exercised there — prefill unaffected by design). Decode path (perplexity -ub 1, c128 x 8): base 8.0332, P1 8.0163, P2 8.0358. KL vs saved base logits: A/A mean ≈0 (max 6e-5 storage floor); **P1 mean KLD 2.7e-4, 99% 4.2e-3, max 9.1e-3, top-1 99.6%**; P2 2.0e-4, top-1 99.2%. For scale x86 Q8_0 vs bf16: 3.4e-3, 97.0% (D010). 64-token greedy text byte-identical for all arms.
- Precision note: MMF rounds F32 activations to bf16 before MMA (mmf.cuh:202-212) — a small numerics change, same class the down-projection already has in the base. Not "bit-exact"; passes the D005 smoke gate and a token-level check.
- Limits: one host, one model/precision, batch 1 decode, MAXN_SUPER with dynamic GPU devfreq (not pinned); only 2 runs per arm (each 5 reps) — effect (≈+10 t/s) ≫ A/A spread (≤0.3 t/s). Unknown on quantized weights (Q8_0/Q4 take MMVQ, different path), on multi-sequence decode, on other cc.
- Next discriminating experiment (x86): drop the `cc == 870` guard (or add cc 1200) and run the same A/B on the 5070 Ti — whether discrete Blackwell has the same MMVF-vs-MMF gap is unknown.
EOF
mkdir -p cc/moe_dispatch_sm87 && cat >> cc/moe_dispatch_sm87/README.md <<'EOF'

---
# Component CC: `moe-gateup-mmf` (status: qualified on jetson-arm; untested elsewhere) — added by Opus after J-E005
**What:** env-gated change to llama.cpp CUDA dispatch: for bf16 MUL_MAT_ID single-token decode, skip the fused gate/up+GLU MMVF kernel and run gate and up through MMF (tensor cores) + separate GLU. Result on Jetson Orin Nano: decode +19%, KLD 2.7e-4 (decisions/D025).
**Integrate:** Build CC `--patch cc/moe_dispatch_sm87/patches/01-unfuse-bf16-ids-to-mmf.patch` (or `combined-01-02.patch`) on llama.cpp 31288c9c6; run with `GGML_CUDA_J_MMF_IDS=1`. Default off = upstream behaviour.
**Applicability (declared):** weights bf16; activations/output F32; MUL_MAT_ID with dst->ne[2]==1 (one token); MMF-eligible shape (K divisible by 64, rows divisible by 32 — Granite gate/up 1024x512 ok); compute capability exactly 870 as written. Not applicable: quantized weights (MMVQ path), AMD, prefill (ne[2]>1 never fused).
**State/sync:** stateless; no new buffers; CUDA graphs unaffected (flag read once per process, static).
**Tests (must run per consumer image):** (1) tg128 A/B counterbalanced vs same image without env; (2) `llama-perplexity -c 128 --chunks 8 -b 128 -ub 1` KL vs saved base logits (gate: mean KLD < 1e-3, top-1 ≥ 99%); (3) 64-token greedy generation diff; (4) nsys kernel inventory shows 2× MMF per layer-token and no dropped kernels.
**Known counterexample/limits:** patch 02 (MMVF block 128) is unreachable when 01 is active and MMF-eligible (review finding); it is a fallback for MMF-ineligible shapes only.
EOF

file.content:
# Lab Manager design (derived from campaign operations; living document)
Scope: deterministic coordination only (no reasoning agent). The other team owns the lab agent / sandbox provisioning; our reference adapter is a TEMPORARY Docker-container stand-in (`bin/lab`), never claimed to be their lab.

## Responsibility map
| Actor | Owns | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Builder (coding sandbox) | source edits, patches, build CC invocations | builds/results/*/build-record.json |
| Build CC | source+patch+bases -> runtime image + archive + record (incl. failures) | W4 attempt 1 failure record |
| Lab Manager (controller) | immutable job spec, attempts, admission, ownership token, state log, export, registration, reconcile | lab/jobs/*, LAB-FEASIBILITY.md |
| Lab agent (other team) | accept/reject/needs-info, choose+provision sandbox | NOT exercised |
| Test sandbox | runs ONE test container per request; disposable; no docker socket; RO model/data | job CR1-crash |
| Evidence store | outside sandbox: stdout/stderr streamed to files, state.jsonl, export w/ MANIFEST | lab/export/* |

## Demonstrated behaviors (op/job refs)
idempotent submit + conflicting-spec rejection (job-3d376c81fb); attempts/retry-as-new (job-9252e2d8bf att-2; job-3739814377 att-2); cancel requested != confirmed (job-93d03ebe43); runner death -> orphan container found by label+token and killed (job-e91db9b081); death during export -> resume, no rescoring (D006 fix, job-5bbc09b093); late conflicting / foreign-token result rejected (cases 4a/4b); duplicate delivery during active attempt rejected rc 8 and replacement blocked until owner gone/reconciled (job-3739814377); controlled sandbox kill -> interrupted_sandbox_terminated with coverage, never pass, controller responsive (job-3739814377 att-1).

## Open / not demonstrated
Admission/queueing (user removed lock D007: single-job-at-a-time is procedural; no capacity model), leases/heartbeats (deliberately not used: liveness = pid+start-time and labelled containers), runner timeouts, disk/capture budgets, retention/GC, remote receiver acknowledgement states (received/accepted/rejected/needs-information are specified in engine_handoff but not yet exchanged with a real lab agent), host-loss failure domain (protected domain = sandbox/process only; evidence on same host).

## Additions from the memory-objective phase (D012-D015)
Demonstrated (job/op refs): image admission by archive: wrong sha256 -> rc 10, wrong expected config id after load -> rc 12, correct -> admitted (op "image-load b0 archive", builds/results/b0-baseline-3); Build CC emitted a patched engine in 18 s via ccache cache mount (builds/results/rt1) vs 7-11 min clean (b0-baseline-2: 11-min build lost to a link error; recorded as failed attempt with stage + full log); per-test memory sampling (GPU peak via nvidia-smi, container cgroup memory.peak and io.stat) with own-file cold cache and container memory limits (job-6e6b2d39b8); test definitions as data (lab/tests/*.json) with per-test env, model file, docker mounts, memory limit.
New requirements found by failure:
- R-A **Interface contracts between CCs must be pinned, not described.** The handoff CC (T-E) was given a flat build-record schema; the Build CC (T-D) emitted a nested one; admission refused a genuinely good delivery (experiments/handoff-real/verdict.json). Needed: a versioned build-record schema owned by one place, plus a normalizer test across both. -> Manager/CC-registry concern, not agent reasoning.
- R-B **Observed vs declared must be enforced by the admission tool**: values from the build record are claims; image config id, platform and executable hashes must be re-observed from the archive (T-K).
- R-C **Concurrent work contaminates measurements** even without a GPU lock: build/compile jobs (load avg up to 18/16 threads) distorted CPU-expert speeds (D015). Admission must also cover CPU/IO load or record load average and mark runs contaminated. (GPU lock was removed by the user, D007; this is the observed cost.)
- R-D **Memory is a first-class measurement**: GPU peak + container peak + physical reads, with cold/warm declared per test; a result without a declared cache state is not comparable.
- R-E Delegated agents (Codex x11, Opus x1, Sonnet x1, gpt-6-astra advice x1) required written assignments, write-location scoping and independent re-verification: Codex G's and H's analysis was high quality; Codex-written code passed its own tests but the integration (R-A) failed only when two outputs met.

# Lab core feasibility (campaign c1) — what the prototype `bin/lab` demonstrated
Scope: image = container (immutable id), tests = named definitions run inside it, job = immutable submission, attempt = one execution. No UI. Evidence: lab/jobs/*/att-*/state.jsonl, result.json; ops in evidence/orchestrator.jsonl.

## Demonstrated (ran against real containers + GPU)
| # | Guarantee | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Images bound to immutable id; same name cannot silently point at a different image | `lab image add` check |
| 2 | Idempotent submission by key; same key + different spec rejected; job.json write-protected | job-3d376c81fb dup/conflict |
| 3 | Happy path, 3 tests (ppl2, gen_smoke, bench_pg) in one admitted attempt; ppl2 = 7.5325 matches E001 | job-3d376c81fb/att-1 |
| 4 | Five result sections kept separate (execution / quality / performance / evidence / cleanup) | result.json |
| 5 | Runner SIGKILL mid-test: orphan container found by label+token, killed, attempt `interrupted`, partial stdout kept, NOT scored | job-e91db9b081 |

## Problems found (these drive the interface)
- P1 **Lock != exclusivity.** flock vanished with the dead runner while its container kept using the GPU (case 5). Admission must be tied to the *container's* lifetime / cgroup, or reconcile must precede re-admission.
- P2 **Recovery bug (D006):** first reconcile overwrote a finished result. Recovery must be phase-aware and results write-once. This was found only because the test killed the runner *in each phase*; "runner died" as one test would have missed it.
- P3 **No per-job single-active-attempt policy.** Two invocations of one job = two attempts (case 6). Needs an explicit policy (reject / queue / coalesce).
- P4 **Measurement confound is invisible to the lab:** SM clock at launch was 2955 MHz vs 1155 MHz across attempts; the lab records it but cannot control it. Perf tests need clock/warmup policy declared in the test, not guessed.
- P5 **First-rep warmup** in bench_pg samples (14.9k vs ~18k t/s): raw samples must be kept; averaging hides it.
- P6 **Root-owned outputs:** container ran as root, so converted GGUF is root-owned on the host. Cleanup/export needs a uid policy.
- P7 **Test definitions are code in the lab, not data.** Each new test (parser + assessor) required editing `bin/lab`. A test needs a declarative contract: command, input mounts, parser, assessor, whether it needs exclusive GPU.
- P8 **Wrapper blind spot (D001)** repeated at a larger scale: process-group tracking insufficient; label+token ownership worked.
- P9 Host-visible only: ownership by docker label can be forged by anyone who can run docker; this is "ownership by convention + token", not enforcement.

## Not demonstrated (proposals only)
Heartbeat/lease handling, timeouts for the *runner* (only per-test timeout), disk/capture budgets, multi-GPU, queue fairness, retention/GC of exports, remote execution, authentication.

# What the Jetson consumer taught the Lab Manager design (for the x86 Manager owner)
Source: host jetson-arm (Orin Nano 8GB, linux/arm64, shared DRAM), branch jetson/c1, 2026-11-10. Read against MANAGER-DESIGN.md and LAB-FEASIBILITY.md.
Class key: [MP] Manager policy | [LA] lab-agent/provider implementation (other team) | [CC-op] reusable CC operation | [COMP] component | [AR] agent reasoning.
Status key: DEMO = ran on Jetson with job evidence; REVIEW = code/unit tests/review only; NOT = not done.
Caveat: the reference adapter is bin/lab (temporary Docker stand-in). Everything below describes it, not the other team's lab. No real lab agent was exercised.

## 1. Host capability inventory and admission decisions
- Event: lab/hosts/{x86-main,jetson-arm}.json (host_id, platform, gpu.{request,sampler,memory_domain,arch}, resources_max, capabilities, l4t_major). Admission decision recorded per job in admission.json with host_profile_sha256.
  - job-ecf12fd41a: accepted (reasons empty). Real run, completed.
  - job-0ec3b98dbb: rejected: platform mismatch linux/amd64 (x2), cuda_arch mismatch, missing requirement runtime and l4t_major. `bin/lab run` on it exits 10 (op-f8f22d97344c).
  - job-82c4a257d3: needs_information "model path missing". job-c7046d34b6: needs_information "unknown image record nope".
- Design must: make the three-way decision (accepted / rejected = cannot ever fit this host / needs_information = fixable by the submitter) a first-class, durable, per-job record taken BEFORE any attempt, naming the host profile hash it was computed against. `run` must refuse non-accepted jobs. Reasons are machine-readable strings today; they should be codes.
- Class: decision vocabulary, record shape and "no attempt without accepted record" = [MP]. Deciding what a host can run and provisioning = [LA] (their agent owns accept/reject; our rules are a stand-in). Profile content is host-owned data.
- Status: DEMO for the four outcomes above. The admission was a pure function of (image record, spec, host profile, local file existence); no remote negotiation.
- Declared vs locally verified images: `lab image add --declared --platform P` stores image_id=null, verified_locally=false, provenance=declared; admission then yields needs_information "image not verified on this host". Requirements are claims from the build record (target_requirements: platform, cuda_arch, runtime, l4t_major); the arch/platform checks run against the host profile, not against the image. DEMO of the record shape in admissions above; REVIEW for the declared-image path (no real job exercised it by name in the jobs I read). Class: [MP] (declared never equals admitted) + [CC-op] image-load (archive re-observation, already x86 R-B).
- Admission hashing: job.json carries admission_sha256; `run` re-reads admission.json, compares hash (mismatch -> rc 11), then RE-EVALUATES admission against the current image record and host profile and requires accepted. DEMO of the hash recorded: job-4433960e61 queued state carries admission_sha256. REVIEW only for the mismatch path (rc 11) and for re-evaluation; I did not see a job that tripped rc 11.
- Legacy records: jobs without admission.json run as "legacy-unrecorded" (x86 only, and only if the image record has no platform); J-T4-era admission without hash is "recorded-unhashed (pre-J-T4b)" but still re-checked, so an old rejected job stays refused (D023 note). Observed: job-ecf12fd41a, 5c142dd5df, 43ef050ce9 have no admission_sha256 in their queued state (pre-hash era). Design must: version the admission record and never let "missing" read as "accepted". [MP]. Status: REVIEW (code paths), partially DEMO (the unhashed jobs exist; I did not re-run them).

## 2. Platform-specific GPU request (D022)
- Event: D022. Plain `--runtime nvidia` on Jetson: exit 1 "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version". Adding NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all passed the CUDA smoke (Orin CC 8.7, 0/1024 mismatches). Generic arm64 images do not set the env; l4t bases do.
- Design must: the GPU request is a host-profile field (`gpu.request`: gpus-all vs nvidia-runtime-env) expanded by the launcher; the job spec must not hardcode `--gpus`. A CUDA init failure must be classified as "GPU not exposed to container / request missing" candidate, not "driver incompatible".
- Class: request selection = [MP]/host profile; making the launcher apply it = [LA] (their provisioner must do the equivalent); error classification = [COMP] (result classifier). Status: DEMO of the underlying behaviour (D022) and of the request in real jobs (bin/lab gpu_request emits runtime + env; note it uses capabilities=compute,utility, whereas D022's passing smoke used all). The classifier fix is NOT done: nothing in bin/lab re-labels that CUDA error.

## 3. Memory domain and engine defaults derived from free memory (D023)
- Event: job-4433960e61 att-1 gen_smoke (no -c) chose n_ctx=45568; shared-DRAM high-water 6568 MiB vs baseline 1634 MiB on a 7607 MiB device (earlier same test 5647/6288 MiB in job-ecf12fd41a / 43ef050ce9 att-2). Cause is source-supported: llama.cpp fit uses device free memory, which on Tegra is system-available DRAM.
- Design must: host profile declares gpu.memory_domain (shared-dram vs discrete-vram). Any engine default derived from "free device memory" is a host-memory policy on shared-dram; test definitions must pin it (done for Jetson: lab/tests/jetson.json gen_smoke_c2k). Admission should refuse or flag a test that leaves such a default unpinned on a shared-dram host.
- Class: declaring domain, requiring pinned test params = [MP]; the pin itself = test definition data (our side); an allocator cap (cudaMemGetInfo interposer, x86 cc/gpu_budget) = [COMP], untested on Jetson. Status: DEMO of the symptom; fix applied to Jetson tests only. The admission check that flags unpinned defaults is NOT done (memory_domain is recorded in the profile but bin/lab admission does not read it). x86 gen_smoke result also depends on free VRAM; D023 leaves that decision to x86.

## 4. Telemetry scope
- Event: result.json mem for Jetson tests: gpu_peak_mib/gpu_delta_mib = null, shared_dram_peak_mib + scope "system-shared-dram" + gpu_memory_reason "shared DRAM is not GPU memory"; gpu_post = {gpu:null, compute_apps:null, unavailable:[reason]} (all Jetson jobs).
- Design must: telemetry records carry scope; a missing metric is null plus a reason, never 0; "GPU memory" and "shared DRAM" must not share a field; baseline absence is reported.
- Defects found by the J5 runs, fixed later (compare job-ecf12fd41a/5c142dd5df/43ef050ce9 with job-4433960e61):
  - Early jobs report exclusive_before_after=false although compute_apps is unknown (null). That is a false statement. Job-4433960e61 reports null. Rule: exclusivity unknown is null, not false. [MP] + [COMP].
  - Early jobs have shared_dram_baseline_mib=null with "no tegrastats sample available" (sampler had not produced a line yet); job-4433960e61 has baseline 1634 after a retry-until-sample baseline. Rule: baseline is required or the result is marked baseline-missing. [COMP].
  - Note even now, "exclusivity" for any host is only "no compute apps at end"; during-run interference is not observed (bin/lab says so). On Jetson it cannot be observed at all through this sampler.
- Class: scope vocabulary and null-with-reason rules = [MP]; backends (tegrastats/nvml/cgroup) = [COMP] cc/resource_observe (schema resource-observe/0 proposed as common contract); a provider must supply an equivalent = [LA]. Status: DEMO (both fix and defect); the CC's backends are unit-tested; I did not verify its tests here.
- Sampler lifecycle: tegrastats is a child of the runner; SIGKILL cannot run handlers, so reconcile kills it by recorded pid+start-time (owner.json tegrastats_pid). REVIEW only; owner.json of job-43ef050ce9 att-1 shows no tegrastats fields (runner killed before sampler recording or before that code), so the orphan-sampler cleanup was not demonstrated by that job.

## 5. Crash semantics observed
- Sandbox kill (job-5c142dd5df att-1, op-a9edfb1d8dbd chaos): container exit 137 -> state sandbox_terminated -> execution "interrupted_sandbox_terminated", ppl null, coverage tests_expected 2 / started 1 / completed_cleanly 0, "incomplete data is never scored", partial stdout/stderr hashed in evidence.files, cleanup confirmed. Export reported hash-valid (checkpoint-1; I did not re-hash it). att-2 (retry as new attempt) completed with ppl 10.0094. Class: state names and never-score-incomplete = [MP]; killing the sandbox and reporting it = [LA]. DEMO.
- Runner SIGKILL (job-43ef050ce9 att-1, op-8255cfa1c2cc status signaled): last durable state "running"; immediate rerun refused rc 8 "still active ... no duplicate execution" (op-1a37540ab664); `lab reconcile` then wrote reconciler=true exporting/terminal, execution "interrupted", killed [] (container had already exited, nothing to kill), partial files kept, unscored; rerun created att-2 which completed. Class: single-active-attempt policy, reconcile-before-retry, results write-once = [MP] (resolves x86 P3); who runs reconcile and when = [LA]/[MP] interface (nothing automatic: a human/agent invoked it). DEMO.
- Not exercised on Jetson: death during export, late conflicting/foreign-token registration, cancel. x86 demonstrated these; Jetson lab code is shared, not independently tested. Reconcile with the sampler alive was not tested.

## 6. Evidence durability limits
- Export dir and job state live on the same host as the runner. Verified failure domain: test-sandbox loss only (5c142dd5df). Jetson host loss, disk loss and SD/NVMe failure lose evidence; git is the only cross-host link (evidence/jetson-arm/*.jsonl, handoff docs). There is no live endpoint, no receipt, no acknowledgement. D024: evidence/results can reach git by accident (bulk build outputs nearly pushed, caught at push). Class: durability tiers, "received/accepted" acknowledgement states, retention = [MP] design + [LA] implementation (remote store). Status: NOT done; documented limits only.
- Manager should state per result a durability level (sandbox-survivable / host-local / replicated) rather than imply one. Evidence records must not be assumed present on the x86 host; the x86 view of a Jetson job today is whatever was committed.

## 7. Image identity under the Docker containerd store
- Event: image id in jobs = sha256:0b6c97b1... (job.json image_id). checkpoint-1 and bin/lab archive_ids: with the containerd snapshotter `.Id` is the manifest/index digest, not the config digest; RepoDigests holds a non-pullable local name@digest. bin/lab imageload therefore compares the loaded id to the archive's top-level index digest, and separately the archive's config digest.
- Design must: name digests by role: local_image_digest (what docker reports as Id on this host), config_digest (read from the archive), registry_digest (only after a push, otherwise absent). Never use RepoDigests as evidence of pullability. Immutable binding image name -> id remains (lab image add refuses rebinding).
- Class: envelope field names = [MP] (x86 owns the Build CC envelope, D016 follow-up); archive re-observation = [CC-op]. Status: DEMO that imageload works with the index-digest rule on Jetson (image used by all jobs); the field renaming is a request, NOT done. Jetson image archive sha256 323c787c... for jetson-c1 (note: job image_id above is the local id of the loaded image).

## 8. Build cache keying friction
- Event: J-T1b ccache fix (commit 5459da3 message; I did not re-read the fix) and the cost gap: first Jetson native build 52 min; patched rebuilds are cheap only with ccache. x86 saw 18 s vs 7-11 min (MANAGER-DESIGN D012-D015).
- Observed friction (from commit/checkpoint text, not re-measured here): cache keys depend on paths/host toolchain, so a different host or builder cannot reuse x86 caches, and an arm64 JetPack builder is host-native. Design must: treat build cache as per-(host, toolchain, target) state declared in the Build CC record, never a correctness input; record cache hit/miss. Class: [CC-op]/[COMP]. Status: PARTIAL (works on Jetson per commit 5459da3; cross-host cache sharing NOT done and probably not wanted).

## 9. Per-host single GPU slot
- Event: one integrated GPU, one 7.6 GB shared DRAM pool, no compute-app enumeration. Concurrency was never tested; D007 removed the lock and bin/lab prints "admission: none (gpu lock removed by user decision)" in every attempt. D023 shows a single test already consumes ~6.5 of 7.6 GB, so two concurrent jobs would OOM or contaminate each other (x86 R-C).
- Design must: host profile declares gpu_slots (=1 here) and a host memory budget; the Manager serialises attempts per host (queue or reject) and the rc-8 duplicate guard is only per job. Today the exclusivity is procedural. Class: slot count and queueing = [MP]; enforcement on the host = [LA]. Status: NOT done; the single-active-attempt guard is per-job only.

## Minimum Manager changes requested from x86
- Add an admission record (accepted / rejected / needs_information, coded reasons, host_profile_sha256, record version) as a precondition for any attempt; absent record never means accepted; keep re-evaluation at run time.
- Host profile schema: platform, gpu.request, gpu.sampler, gpu.memory_domain, arch, resources_max, gpu_slots; submit gets host_id; GPU request is expanded from the profile.
- Telemetry contract (resource-observe/0 or successor): scope field, null + reason for unavailable, required baseline, exclusivity as true/false/null (unknown never false).
- Result classifier: CUDA init failures on Jetson-style hosts must be reported as "GPU not exposed" candidates; never as driver mismatch.
- Rule that engine defaults depending on free memory are pinned by the test on shared-dram hosts; decide whether x86 gen_smoke pins -c (D023).
- Image identity fields by role (local_image_digest, config_digest, registry_digest); stop treating RepoDigests as pullable.
- Per-result durability level and a defined remote receipt (received / accepted / rejected / needs_information) before claiming cross-host evidence; keep the single-active-attempt + reconcile-before-retry rule from job-43ef050ce9.
- Per-host slot/queue policy (1 slot on Jetson) instead of the removed global lock.

## Explicitly not needed / avoid
- No host-specific branches in the Manager (if jetson ...); everything via profile fields.
- Do not pool or compare raw Jetson and x86 numbers (different weights file hashes bb010fb6 vs af76ade0, different domain); keep results per host.
- No heartbeats/leases for Jetson reasons; pid+start-time plus label/token ownership sufficed in job-43ef050ce9.
- Do not make agent reasoning part of admission; the observed decisions were deterministic functions of record + profile.

# What the Jetson consumer taught the Lab Manager design (for the x86 Manager owner)

Admission should refuse or flag a test that leaves such a default unpinned on a shared-dram host.

  - Early jobs report exclusive_before_after=false although compute_apps is unknown (null). That is a false statement. Job-4433960e61 reports null. Rule: exclusivity unknown is null, not false. [MP] + [COMP].
  - Early jobs have shared_dram_baseline_mib=null with "no tegrastats sample available" (sampler had not produced a line yet); job-4433960e61 has baseline 1634 after a retry-until-sample baseline. Rule: baseline is required or the result is marked baseline-missing. [COMP].

Status: DEMO (both fix and defect); the CC's backends are unit-tested; I did not verify its tests here.

- Sandbox kill (job-5c142dd5df att-1, op-a9edfb1d8dbd chaos): container exit 137 -> state sandbox_terminated -> execution "interrupted_sandbox_terminated", ppl null, coverage tests_expected 2 / started 1 / completed_cleanly 0, "incomplete data is never scored", partial stdout/stderr hashed in evidence.files, cleanup confirmed. Export reported hash-valid (checkpoint-1; I did not re-hash it). att-2 (retry as new attempt) completed with ppl 10.0094. Class: state names and never-score-incomplete = [MP]; killing the sandbox and reporting it = [LA]. DEMO.

Class: single-active-attempt policy, reconcile-before-retry, results write-once = [MP] (resolves x86 P3); who runs reconcile and when = [LA]/[MP] interface (nothing automatic: a human/agent invoked it). DEMO.

D024: evidence/results can reach git by accident (bulk build outputs nearly pushed, caught at push). Class: durability tiers, "received/accepted" acknowledgement states, retention = [MP] design + [LA] implementation (remote store). Status: NOT done; documented limits only.
- Manager should state per result a durability level (sandbox-survivable / host-local / replicated) rather than imply one. Evidence records must not be assumed present on the x86 host; the x86 view of a Jetson job today is whatever was committed.

- Event: image id in jobs = sha256:0b6c97b1... Status: DEMO that imageload works with the index-digest rule on Jetson (image used by all jobs); the field renaming is a request, NOT done. - Event: J-T1b ccache fix (commit 5459da3 message; I did not re-read the fix) and the cost gap: first Jetson native build 52 min; patched rebuilds are cheap only with ccache. x86 saw 18 s vs 7-11 min (MANAGER-DESIGN D012-D015).

Status: PARTIAL (works on Jetson per commit 5459da3; cross-host cache sharing NOT done and probably not wanted).

## 9. Per-host single GPU slot
- Event: one integrated GPU, one 7.6 GB shared DRAM pool, no compute-app enumeration. Concurrency was never tested; D007 removed the lock and bin/lab prints "admission: none (gpu lock removed by user decision)" in every attempt. D023 shows a single test already consumes ~6.5 of 7.6 GB, so two concurrent jobs would OOM or contaminate each other (x86 R-C).
- Design must: host profile declares gpu_slots (=1 here) and a host memory budget; the Manager serialises attempts per host (queue or reject) and the rc-8 duplicate guard is only per job. Today the exclusivity is procedural. Class: slot count and queueing = [MP]; enforcement on the host = [LA]. Status: NOT done; the single-active-attempt guard is per-job only.

## Minimum Manager changes requested from x86
- Add an admission record (accepted / rejected / needs_information, coded reasons, host_profile_sha256, record version) as a precondition for any attempt; absent record never means accepted; keep re-evaluation at run time.
- Host profile schema: platform, gpu.request, gpu.sampler, gpu.memory_domain, arch, resources_max, gpu_slots; submit gets host_id; GPU request is expanded from the profile.
- Telemetry contract (resource-observe/0 or successor): scope field, null + reason for unavailable, required baseline, exclusivity as true/false/null (unknown never false).
- Result classifier: CUDA init failures on Jetson-style hosts must be reported as "GPU not exposed" candidates; never as driver mismatch.
- Rule that engine defaults depending on free memory are pinned by the test on shared-dram hosts; decide whether x86 gen_smoke pins -c (D023).
- Image identity fields by role (local_image_digest, config_digest, registry_digest); stop treating RepoDigests as pullable.
- Per-result durability level and a defined remote receipt (received / accepted / rejected / needs_information) before claiming cross-host evidence; keep the single-active-attempt + reconcile-before-retry rule from job-43ef050ce9.
- Per-host slot/queue policy (1 slot on Jetson) instead of the removed global lock.

## Explicitly not needed / avoid
- No host-specific branches in the Manager (if jetson ...); everything via profile fields.
- Do not pool or compare raw Jetson and x86 numbers (different weights file hashes bb010fb6 vs af76ade0, different domain); keep results per host.
- No heartbeats/leases for Jetson reasons; pid+start-time plus label/token ownership sufficed in job-43ef050ce9.
- Do not make agent reasoning part of admission; the observed decisions were deterministic functions of record + profile.
- Do not assume Jetson GPU memory numbers exist; do not synthesise zeros for them.

name: jetson-lane-ops
description: Operational gotchas for running the siminfeng campaign on the Jetson host (codex, docker, builds, git)
metadata:

---
Host `satay` = lane `jetson-arm` (Orin Nano 8GB, L4T R36.5.2); work goes on branch `jetson/c1` pushed to origin (never main). Host id file: ~/.config/siminfeng/host_id.

- `codex exec` must get `< /dev/null` when backgrounded, else it exits immediately ("Reading additional input from stdin").
- Docker needs `sg docker -c "..."` in sessions predating group membership; lab/Build CC use env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX='sg docker -c'`.
- sudo needs a password the agent can't type; the user runs sudo in their own terminal.
- Never `git add` a directory a running build writes to; Build CC outputs under cc/build_engine/results/*/{build,staging-*,*.tar} are gitignored (D024 near-miss).
- Jetson images need `--runtime nvidia` even for CPU tools (all link libcuda); host build/bin needs LD_LIBRARY_PATH (RUNPATH points to deleted staging).
- Pin `-c` in Jetson tests: llama.cpp auto-fit eats shared DRAM (D023).

**Why:** each cost a failed attempt this campaign. **How to apply:** check before launching workers/builds/commits on this host. Related: [[user-cost-preference]]
