# Router-informed expert mmap prefetch (J-OM7)

`patches/02-router-prefetch.patch` applies after `patches/01-mmap-advice-random.patch` to `ref/llama.cpp-up1108` at `cf34d3113`. The reference checkout is unchanged. This is a Linux-only, opt-in experiment; no build or GPU execution was performed for this assignment.

```bash
cat cc/mmap_advice/patches/01-mmap-advice-random.patch \
    cc/mmap_advice/patches/02-router-prefetch.patch > /tmp/om7-combined.patch
git -C ref/llama.cpp-up1108 apply --check /tmp/om7-combined.patch
```

## Mechanism

Set `LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH=1`. The loader supplies the file ranges of `ffn_*_exps.weight` tensors as mmap advice exclusions, separately from the existing lazy-loading placement policy. These ranges receive `MADV_RANDOM` and are excluded from initial `WILLNEED` and `MAP_POPULATE`; non-expert ranges retain default sequential file advice and initial `WILLNEED`. Existing lazy ranges remain excluded. Expert mode takes precedence over `LLAMA_MMAP_ADVICE=random`, so that setting both does not make the entire file random. With expert mode off, patch 01 retains its original behavior. NUMA and other explicit loading policies still apply.

The scheduler's new CPU-only before-node callback observes the first `MUL_MAT_ID` that uses a layer's original expert weights. Its `src[2]` is the same `ffn_moe_topk-L` I32 tensor named in `src/llama-graph.cpp:2367`, or the scheduler's host copy of that tensor. CPU graph prefixes finish before observation. The callback reads `{K,T,1,1}` with the actual strides, validates IDs, and deduplicates all selected IDs across the ubatch. Before that expert matmul starts, it issues `madvise(MADV_WILLNEED)` for each ID's gate/up/down slice (also supports merged gate-up). Each slice uses `data + id * nb[2]`, length `nb[2]`, aligned outward to OS pages. Qwen's observed gate/up slices are 589,824 bytes and down slices 720,896 bytes; the implementation derives sizes from tensors, including exceptional layers.

Only contiguous three-dimensional expert tensors whose entire actual data span is inside a model-owned mmap are eligible. A host buffer alone is insufficient proof. Unsupported tensors or router layouts are skipped with a once-per-context log. Biases/scales, transformed router IDs, and MoE-cache slot IDs are not interpreted as original expert IDs. No model weights, router IDs, or floating-point operations are modified.

Each layer retains at most 32 advised IDs in an LRU, with a 32-token expiry measured in that layer's ubatch token count. Cache hits update recency without extending the last-advice timestamp. Failed advice is counted and does not suppress a later retry. A large ubatch is one deduplicated observation; expiry is evaluated at its end, not separately for each token. This is a syscall limiter, not a page-residency tracker.

`LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH_NEXT=1` additionally advises the same union of IDs in layer L+1, subject to its expert bounds and the same LRU. It has no effect without the primary switch. When L+1 is observed in the same ubatch, each distinct prediction counts once in `total`, and membership in its actual selected union counts as a hit. This is prediction precision over ubatch unions, not per-token accuracy; large prompts can inflate it. Predictions whose next layer is never host-observed are excluded from the ratio and are cleared at the next ubatch. No last-layer wraparound occurs.

At context destruction, after synchronization, `LLAMA_LOG_INFO` reports attempted advice calls, attempted page-rounded bytes, syscall failures, and next-layer prediction hits/total plus percent. Bytes advised are hints, not measured disk bytes. Startup logs identify both mapping policy and the host-consumer hook; zero calls must not be treated as evidence of active prefetch.

## Applicability and synchronization

Works with mmap-backed CPU experts under CPU-only execution or any GPU/CPU layer split, including `-ngl 99 -cmoe`. `-cmoe` moves expert weights/operations to CPU; it does **not** force router computation to CPU. With GPU-offloaded layers, router top-k can be GPU-computed. The scheduler already copies these IDs to the CPU expert split and waits for that copy (including its existing asynchronous prefetch event). Observation occurs at this first host consumer, after those existing waits. It does not request another readback or synchronize a GPU backend. The added synchronization is CPU-only; the existing CPU backend's graph compute is already synchronous and its synchronize function is null.

The regular scheduler eval callback is preserved, including its existing synchronization behavior. Installing an ordinary eval callback just to read GPU top-k would introduce a synchronization; this patch avoids that path. On all-CPU execution it finishes the prefix containing the router before reading IDs. On GPU routing it deliberately defers observation from top-k production to the first CPU expert consumer. Device-only expert paths are skipped instead of creating a new device-to-host dependency. GPU-uploaded weights, non-mmap loads, unsupported layouts, and cached/remapped IDs receive no exact host prefetch. Non-Linux builds do not enable the feature.

## Risks

`WILLNEED` is a best-effort kernel hint and may start late, block briefly, or fail; it does not guarantee expert-sized physical IO. Page rounding can include neighboring weights. Predictions and stale LRU entries can waste IO or suppress useful rereads after eviction. Even exact advice may compete with current reads and evict useful cache pages. The CPU graph prefix boundary adds planning/threadpool overhead. Applying RANDOM to experts also changes initial model upload behavior for offloaded weights; measure startup separately. The feature has not been compiled or performance-validated. D033's speedup estimate is a hypothesis, not a result.

## A/B/C for the build/run owner (jetson-arm)

Use one executable containing 01+02 for all three arms and the same Qwen model, fixed prompt, seed, context, thread counts, ubatch size, and generation length. Reproduce D033 with `-lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe`, 64 generated tokens, and its recorded p1 prompt. Keep the existing telemetry collector running and quiesce unrelated NVMe work. Example arm invocations, after setting `BIN`, `MODEL`, and `PROMPT_FILE`:

```bash
env -u LLAMA_MMAP_ADVICE -u LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH -u LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH_NEXT \
  "$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -f "$PROMPT_FILE" -n 64 -lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe --seed 1 \
  > base.stdout 2> base.stderr
env -u LLAMA_MMAP_ADVICE -u LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH_NEXT LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH=1 \
  "$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -f "$PROMPT_FILE" -n 64 -lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe --seed 1 \
  > prefetch.stdout 2> prefetch.stderr
env -u LLAMA_MMAP_ADVICE LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH=1 LLAMA_EXPERT_PREFETCH_NEXT=1 \
  "$BIN" -m "$MODEL" -f "$PROMPT_FILE" -n 64 -lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe --seed 1 \
  > next.stdout 2> next.stderr
```

## 1. What selects the kernels

**The asymmetry comes from graph fusion, not a special slow standalone gate/up dispatcher.** The fused gate/up+GLU path asks the MMVF heuristic; the ordinary NVIDIA `MUL_MAT_ID` dispatcher instead asks the MMF heuristic. Disabling only the eligible BF16 ID fusion is sufficient to send both projections through the existing MMF implementation.

### Shape and architecture interpretation

For gate/up, weight dimensions are `[1024,512,32,1]`; for down, `[512,1024,32,1]`. The first dimension is the reduction length, the second the output-row count, and the third the number of experts. Eight selected experts are output channels, not eight tokens. ID kernels use `dst->ne[2]` / `src1->ne[2]` for token count: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvf.cu:695-704`, `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmf.cu:55-69`. Thus d

CC is encoded as 870 for sm_87 (Ampere threshold 800): `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:54-66`. `ampere_mma_available` checks NVIDIA plus highest compiled architecture >=800, not just the physical CC: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:369-371`. The interpretation here assumes the Orin build includes Ampere MMA device code, consistent with the observed BF16 MMF kernel.

### Fused gate/up

- `ggml_cuda_should_fuse_mul_mat_vec_f` requires weights F32/F16/BF16, activations/output F32, and calls `ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf` using `src1->ne[2]` for IDs. Fusion requires exactly one token for IDs (`dst->ne[2]==1`), or one output column for ordinary matmul: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:1847-1872`.
- MMVF requires an even reduction length, contiguous dimension zero, and higher strides divisible by twice the weight element size: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvf.cu:791-807`.
- For BF16 NVIDIA, `src0_small = (src0_ne[1] <= 512 || src0_ne[2]*src0_ne[3] == 1)`. The later Ada/non-Ampere branches allow <=4 / <=3 respectively; the Ampere branch takes precedence on sm_87: `ggml/src/ggml-cuda/mmvf.cu:858-875`; maximum d

## Attribution scopes (do NOT sum across scopes)
- `system-shared-dram` (tegrastats RAM): whole-system DRAM shared by CPU and GPU on Jetson.
- `system` (/proc/meminfo): same physical pages viewed system-wide; `process` (VmRSS/VmHWM) and `cgroup` (memory.current/peak/max) are subsets of the same pages. Adding them to tegrastats RAM double counts.
- cgroup metrics carry `accounting_note`: cgroup v2 may not include nvmap/driver GPU allocations on Tegra, so it can under-report GPU memory. Unlimited `memory.max` is reported unavailable. memory.peak may be missing on older kernels (unavailable). This host's cgroup controllers file lists memory.
- `device-discrete` (nvml): dedicated VRAM, x86 only. On Orin nvidia-smi exists but returns [N/A]; backend reports unavailable.
- sysfs_tegra: GPU devfreq (MHz), thermal zones (celsius, unreadable zones listed unavailable), nvpmodel mode (`nvpmodel -q`, query only, or `--nvpmodel-mode`).

No NvMap fields on this kernel's meminfo (reported unavailable); no iomem/debugfs nvmap per-client attribution (needs root); tegrastats gets its own interval, summarize infers interval from median spacing if not given; nvml parsed from CSV fixtures only on this host (no discrete GPU).

## 1. Strata mechanism for models larger than memory

Strata is NOT a generic "stream everything from SSD" engine. It is a 3-tier expert placement: VRAM cache -> RAM (or mmap'd
file pages) -> SSD file tier. Hot experts are on GPU; misses are computed in place by CPU threads in parallel with the GPU.
- Resident on GPU: attention/DeltaNet mixers, routers, shared experts, head, KV (from 64K only its hot part, rest streams
  from RAM), plus an expert cache filling remaining VRAM (docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md:14-25).
- Resident in RAM: all experts, pinned; CPU computes the non-cached ones "in place" concurrently (HOW_IT_WORKS.md:27-29).
- Over-memory regime (the relevant one): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2.00 bpw, 138 GB experts + 111 GB n-gram table. Experts go
  "as many as fit in graphics memory; the rest computed on the CPU, read in place from the model files"; n-gram table stays
  on SSD, a few rows per token (docs/DEEPSEEK41.md:13-17). "With less memory than that, part of the CPU's experts are read

## 1. Pinned vs upstream moe-cache

Common skeleton (both trees; P file 639 lines, U 916):
- Eligibility: a layer is cached only if ALL its expert tensors (gate_up|gate,up,down) are WEIGHTS usage in a host buffer
  (`ggml_backend_buffer_is_host`) - U llama-moe-cache.cpp:312-316, 422-444 (P: same helper at ~150-160). Device type GPU or IGPU
  accepted (U:405) so Orin Nano qualifies. mmap'd CPU buffers count as host.
- Granularity: one slot = one whole expert across all its tensors (bank per tensor, `bank ne[2] = n_slots(+n_zero+1)`; U:553-558).
  Slot size = sum of `t->nb[2]` (gate+up+down or gate_up+down) -> for Q4_K_XL ~ 1.3-1.6 MiB/expert/layer.
- Budget: ONE global budget `--moe-cache-mib` (per device, split by free mem/tensor-split, U:462-483). Within a device, layers with identical
  tensor layout form a `group` that shares ONE bank set and ONE LRU across all layers (U:332-343, 503-519), i.e. a global pool across layers,
  not per-layer. `n_slots` = largest N with padded alloc <= budget (U:508). Must be >= n_expert_used else "not cached" (U:511).
  Hybrid layouts (e.g. different quant per layer) become separate groups, each getting budget proportional to host bytes.
- Slot map: per-layer I32[n_expert] in host memory (U:569). Graph does `get_rows(slot_map, ids)` -> `mul_mat_id(bank_view, cur, slots)`
  (llama-graph.cpp U:2664-2713, 1765). Scheduler copy callback `llama_moe_cache::copy` (U:761-856) fires when the slot-map split is
  copied: D2H-reads selected ids (U:799-800, SYNCHRONIZES the backend each layer), runs `plan()`, uploads misses, uploads slot map (U:853).
  Hook: llama-context.cpp:2991 (copy cb), 3044 (large-batch `copy_experts`, device->device copy of cached experts into the scratch).
- Used only for ubatch <= `max_batch`=32 tokens and when unique experts fit (U:368, 694); bigger batches bypass (read-only reuse via copy_experts).
- Upload path: `ggml_backend_tensor_set_async` -> `cudaMemcpyAsync(H2D)` straight from `w->data + e*nb[2]` (U:840; ggml-cuda.cu:2894-2901).
  Source is the model tensor in place: pageable mmap pages unless weights were loaded pinned. NO staging buffer of its own; consecutive
  expert+slot pairs are merged into one memcpy (U:835-843). Sorted miss order gives mergeable runs (U:270).

- P: plain LRU (single doubly-linked list; `plan` P:74-109): hits touched to tail, misses sorted, victim = head, no admission control, no

# Digest of x86 D041-D048 for the Jetson over-memory lane (2026-11-10)
Source: `origin/x86/c2-resume` (`START-HERE.md` section 0, `decisions/D041..D048`). x86 hardware is an RTX 5070 Ti (16 GB VRAM, discrete, PCIe 4.0) plus a Ryzen 7 3700X, models Qwen3-30B-A3B Q4_K_M and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. Do not pool t/s across hosts.
Jetson context: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B UD-Q4_K_XL (22.4 GB) on 7.4 GiB shared DRAM, ~570 MiB/s NVMe, `-lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe`, decode 1.2-1.36 t/s, disk-bound: decode ~ disk_BW / (615 MB x miss_rate); page-cache LRU hit ~62% (see Jetson D030-D033). Key structural difference: x86 "cache" is a VRAM cache over host RAM (PCIe-bound, 1.5-28 GB/s links); ours is page cache over NVMe (disk-bound, 0.57 GB/s) with no CPU/GPU split (UMA).

## D041 (indicative): upstream `--moe-cache-mib` on Qwen3-30B; ncu roofline
- Result: at 8 GB cache beats static `--n-cpu-moe` by +38% decode (51 vs 37 t/s), at 4 GB loses 34% (18 vs 28); upload-only cache needs ~70-75% hit rate. ncu: 222 GB/s, 40% of kernel time in tiny kernels.
- Jetson relevance: consistent with our Jetson D030 (upstream moe-cache loses on UMA at 64% hits). The "hit rate >= ~75% to win" threshold matches; we are below it at 62%. Nothing new to run.

## D042 (indicative): n-gram self-spec, perf, bpftrace, intake
- Result: `--spec-type ngram-mod` on Qwen3-30B K30: 2.4x (rewrite) / 3.0x (repeat), text identical, 0 drafts and +-0% on open chat. perf: no DRAM-bandwidth PMU on Zen 2. bpftrace: 0.79 ms/CPU layer. Rule: log `draft_n`/`draft_n_accepted`; benchmark bandwidth with working set >= 8x LLC.
- Jetson relevance: n-gram is a flag, no rebuild if our image's llama-server has `--spec-type` (pin 31288c9c6 is the same engine x86 used). Costs nothing on chat. Verify batch reads each expert once per batch, which is the lever for a disk-bound decoder (see analysis below). Bandwidth-microbenchmark rule applies to our fio ceiling (we already model 570 MiB/s, Jetson D031).

## D043 / D047: protocols (no results)
- Frozen overnight protocols; amendments: A1 download A/A (0.2% effect), A2 post-hoc decode-path KLD (ub 1). Rule: a batch-shape floor (KLD ~0.0058, top-1 ~96.5-97%) exists for the reference itself; gate equivalence against it, not text identity.
- Jetson relevance: adopt the same KLD floor language; our D025/D027 gates (KLD 2.7e-4) already well inside it. Add swap/page-fault monitoring to quiet checks, which our watchdog already does.

## D044 (speed rule met): cache + CPU-share beats static at 4/6/8/10 GB
- Result: C3 (cache + `--moe-cache-cpu-share 0.9`) beats static by +30..+76% at every budget with 3-6% less VRAM; hit rate 50%/73%/87%/92% at 4/6/8/10 GB; share 0 is best above ~90% hit; TTFT worse (prompt eval does not use cache). Absolute KLD gate was miscalibrated.
- Jetson relevance: CPU-share exists to compute misses on the CPU instead of uploading over PCIe. On UMA the "upload" is a no-op (D030 found the cache duplicates residency) and the miss cost is a disk read, so CPU-share does not help. Not worth running. The hit-rate-vs-budget curve is still a useful comparator for our replay sweep (LRU 62% @ 12.7% of model).

- Result: static K30 ngram 2.32x/3.01x text identical, chat +1%; on cache arm 1.53x/1.68x (verify window touches ~19 distinct experts/layer for 4 drafts, extras are misses); cache + ngram 3.9x over static on repeat. Cache arm text depends on cache history. REAP-15B (pruned Qwen3-30B): all-GP

## 5. Lab Manager / CC portfolio discovery

### 5.1 Tools and commands used
bin/run_op (recorded commands; intent/started/outcome, survivors), bin/cc_hook, bin/lab (image add/submit/run/reconcile, host profiles + admission), bin/perf_summary, bin/ledger_appendix.py, cc/build_engine (target jetson-orin, ccache, `--extra-target`, `--with-tests`), cc/resource_observe (tegrastats/proc/cgroup/sysfs/io + watchdog), cc/om_run/om_run.sh (+ pipeline2-6, sweep_*.sh, build_queue.sh, fio_ceiling.sh), cc/expert_replay, cc/routing_trace (generic patch), cc/model_manifest/gguf_manifest.py, llama-bench / llama-perplexity (`--kl-divergence`, `-ub 1`) / llama-completion / llama-quantize, nsys (`--force-export=true` needed when a stale .sqlite gives a 0-byte CSV), tegrastats, fio, ccache 4.5.1, cmake/ninja from pip in ~/.local, docker + buildx, `codex exec` workers, git (`filter-branch` rescue, D024).

### 5.2 Missing tools and repeated manual work
- No "wait for job" primitive: every chain is a hand-written bash pipeline polling `pgrep -f` (pipeline2-6, build_queue). It broke once (5.6).
- Per-run summary extraction written as ad-hoc Python inline in pipelines (prompt/eval t/s from stderr, NVMe GiB and KiB/IO from telemetry, MemAvailable min, output sha) - candidate "run summarizer" CC.
- Flag capability probing: llama-bench lacks `-c`, `-cmoe`, `-mmp`; 11 attempts failed on flags (J-E003 x4, base-0435 x6, feas-b1 x1). Needs a `--help` capability probe before a queued run.
- Switch-effect verification: the NUMA switch was inert; only a log/counter line proved patch advice active. Need a standard "switch active" assertion per env-gated component.
- No A/A-aware acceptance gate in perf_summary yet (Strata autotune rule noted: median per-round ratio > max(3%, 2 x A/A gap, 2 x drift)).
- No launch identity record of the effective engine config (argv is recorded, effective config is not).
- Hand ordering of ABBA/ABAB arms and manual overlap avoidance with builds.
- Telemetry `host_id` field is the hostname (`satay`), not the campaign host id (`jetson-arm`) (D029; fix pending).
- Result classifier labels `watchdog_killed` while exit_code is 0 (feas-b1-a2).

### 5.3 Build and dependency problems
- System numpy is broken on Jetson; heavy converters run from `~/venvs/convert` (torch/transformers). Python tools stay stdlib.
- ccache first attempt had 0/454 hits because staging paths were random; fixed in J-T1b (CCACHE_BASEDIR, NOHASHDIR, compilercheck=content): rebuild 348/360 hits, 141 s vs 3154 s (D026). Binaries still differ per attempt (embedded `staging-...` path); `-ffile-prefix-map` not attempted.
- Docker installed by owner (docker.io 29.1.3, nvidia-ctk runtime); user is in group docker only for new sessions, so old sessions use `sg docker -c` (env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX='sg docker -c'`). buildx is a user plugin (v0.29.1).
- Host-built binaries have RUNPATH to deleted staging dirs, need `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; images need `--runtime nvidia` even for CPU tools.
- Each archive ~1.39 GB; disk 88 GB free at inventory, ~62 GB later with a 22 GB model.
- D024: `git add` of a directory a build was writing nearly published a 1.4 GB archive.
- Nix rejected (Strata flake x86_64 only).

### 5.4 Permissions
sudo needs a password the agent cannot type (owner runs sudo). `ncu` counters blocked (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1). `jetson_clocks`/nvpmodel changes never run, so GPU clocks float (306-1020 MHz); mitigated with warm-up discard and counterbalanced A/B. Docker group, nvidia runtime config and apt installs were owner-authorized (D022).

### 5.5 Platform and memory
- Shared DRAM: no separate VRAM; NVML/nvidia-smi memory is [N/A]; per-client nvmap not visible; never sum `system-shared-dram` with process/cgroup scopes.
- cgroup/`--memory` cap does not bound CUDA allocations (D028); admission budget must say `guarantee: none-for-device-allocations`.
- llama.cpp auto-fit sizes context from "available memory", which on Tegra is system DRAM: unpinned `-c` picked n_ctx 45568 and 6568 MiB high-water (D023). Pin `-c`.
- `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` (+ `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES`) must be set explicitly for generic arm64 images; otherwise "CUDA driver version insufficient" (D022).
- `-lm auto` disables mmap on iGPU (llama-model.cpp:1590, ggml-cuda.cu:5473), so default over-memory runs die; baseline must say `-lm mmap`.
- Zram swap bursts trip naive swap-rate watchdogs (false positives at 33 and 286 MiB/s); limits settled at MemAvailable < 600 MiB, zram > 2.5 GiB, swap rate 1000 MiB/s (cmp sweep), two consecutive samples.
- Storage: 128 GB budget NVMe at ~570 MiB/s is a first-order design input; record drive model + fio matrix in every host inventory (D031).

### 5.6 Scheduling and logging
- One GPU job at a time; builds must not overlap timed runs (D029 unscored; D030/D031 contaminated by nice-19 replay).
- **pipeline4 deadlock**: the wait loop `while pgrep -f "python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py|...pipeline3.sh|...pipeline2.sh"` matched the launching shell's own command line (per the comment in pipeline5.sh), so the loop never ended. The GPU idled about 8.7 h (06:34 to 15:15 on 2026-11-10) and the kernel-screen stage never ran. Fix: wait on a PID (`while kill -0 <PID>`; pipeline6.sh does this); pipeline5.sh was rewritten without pgrep.
- Logging: run_op records intent/started/outcome with host_id; per-host evidence streams `evidence/jetson-arm/` (D021, host id from untracked ~/.config/siminfeng/host_id); run_op non-UTF-8 echo crash fixed (rc 0 reported as 1); telemetry JSONL ~3 MB per 3-minute trace run (bulk, not for git).
- Networking/transport: no SSH between hosts; exchange is git branches `jetson/*` pushed by the operator; evidence durability is sandbox-survivable only (host loss loses data). x86 has not answered round 2.

### 5.7 Recovery
Sandbox kill, runner SIGKILL, duplicate refusal, reconcile, retry-as-new-attempt all demonstrated on Jetson (3.x/2.3). Watchdog kill quoting bug (D029): `--kill-cmd "sg docker -c docker kill NAME"` was split by shlex so `docker` ran bare; fixed with single quotes and a live forced-trip test (watchdog-killtest). Exit codes must come from run_op records, not pipelines (D022: a `| tail` masked a status).

- llama.cpp: `--moe-cache-mib` (#29887), CPU-share (#30966), ClassLRU (#31233), CPU does not wait on cached experts (#31888, in cf34d311). Useful on discrete GPUs (x86 D044: +30..76% over static); a loss on UMA. `test-backend-ops perf` is the cheap screen (needs perf cases added, J-T6). Watch/adopt candidates from the external survey: #31957 (iGPU lazy-mode fallback only when mmap off), #31268/#30858/#28285 (Orin MMVQ), #31469 (study only, qwen4exp-only).
- Strata (MIT, reference): replay policies (LFU-decay, adaptive swap), profile building from a varied corpus, `quant_quality` top-64 renormalised KL, autotune acceptance rule, benchmark protocol IDs, launch identity, management protocol patterns. Engine code does not transfer (own runtime).
- Candidate reuse for the 128 GB / 4 TB target: expert-sized aligned reads and router-informed exact prefetch are the mechanisms worth re-testing on a fast NVMe; the Jetson drive is IOPS-bound.

### Approaches to avoid (evidence-backed)
- `MADV_RANDOM` on the whole model file (D033: half speed).
- Static cross-workload hot sets (leave-one-out 16.6% vs LRU 62.4%).
- Cgroup/`--memory` caps as a GPU or shared-DRAM budget on Tegra (D028).
- `--numa distribute` on a 1-node host as a readahead switch (inert).
- Copying experts into a separate device bank on UMA (D030/D032).
- Treating hit rate as speed on unified memory, batch-512 ppl as a decode-kernel check, binary hash equality as "same build" (D026), raw t/s across hosts.
- Unfusing Q8_0 gate/up on Orin (-6.2%).
- `pgrep -f` wait loops launched from a shell whose command line contains the pattern.

## 5. Lab Manager / CC portfolio discovery

### 5.1 Tools and commands used
bin/run_op (recorded commands; intent/started/outcome, survivors), bin/cc_hook, bin/lab (image add/submit/run/reconcile, host profiles + admission), bin/perf_summary, bin/ledger_appendix.py, cc/build_engine (target jetson-orin, ccache, `--extra-target`, `--with-tests`), cc/resource_observe (tegrastats/proc/cgroup/sysfs/io + watchdog), cc/om_run/om_run.sh (+ pipeline2-6, sweep_*.sh, build_queue.sh, fio_ceiling.sh), cc/expert_replay, cc/routing_trace (generic patch), cc/model_manifest/gguf_manifest.py, llama-bench / llama-perplexity (`--kl-divergence`, `-ub 1`) / llama-completion / llama-quantize, nsys (`--force-export=true` needed when a stale .sqlite gives a 0-byte CSV), tegrastats, fio, ccache 4.5.1, cmake/ninja from pip in ~/.local, docker + buildx, `codex exec` workers, git (`filter-branch` rescue, D024).

### 5.2 Missing tools and repeated manual work
- No "wait for job" primitive: every chain is a hand-written bash pipeline polling `pgrep -f` (pipeline2-6, build_queue). It broke once (5.6).
- Per-run summary extraction written as ad-hoc Python inline in pipelines (prompt/eval t/s from stderr, NVMe GiB and KiB/IO from telemetry, MemAvailable min, output sha) - candidate "run summarizer" CC.
- Flag capability probing: llama-bench lacks `-c`, `-cmoe`, `-mmp`; 11 attempts failed on flags (J-E003 x4, base-0435 x6, feas-b1 x1). Needs a `--help` capability probe before a queued run.
- Switch-effect verification: the NUMA switch was inert; only a log/counter line proved patch advice active. Need a standard "switch active" assertion per env-gated component.
- No A/A-aware acceptance gate in perf_summary yet (Strata autotune rule noted: median per-round ratio > max(3%, 2 x A/A gap, 2 x drift)).
- No launch identity record of the effective engine config (argv is recorded, effective config is not).
- Hand ordering of ABBA/ABAB arms and manual overlap avoidance with builds.
- Telemetry `host_id` field is the hostname (`satay`), not the campaign host id (`jetson-arm`) (D029; fix pending).
- Result classifier labels `watchdog_killed` while exit_code is 0 (feas-b1-a2).

### 5.3 Build and dependency problems
- System numpy is broken on Jetson; heavy converters run from `~/venvs/convert` (torch/transformers). Python tools stay stdlib.
- ccache first attempt had 0/454 hits because staging paths were random; fixed in J-T1b (CCACHE_BASEDIR, NOHASHDIR, compilercheck=content): rebuild 348/360 hits, 141 s vs 3154 s (D026). Binaries still differ per attempt (embedded `staging-...` path); `-ffile-prefix-map` not attempted.
- Docker installed by owner (docker.io 29.1.3, nvidia-ctk runtime); user is in group docker only for new sessions, so old sessions use `sg docker -c` (env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX='sg docker -c'`). buildx is a user plugin (v0.29.1).
- Host-built binaries have RUNPATH to deleted staging dirs, need `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; images need `--runtime nvidia` even for CPU tools.
- Each archive ~1.39 GB; disk 88 GB free at inventory, ~62 GB later with a 22 GB model.
- D024: `git add` of a directory a build was writing nearly published a 1.4 GB archive.
- Nix rejected (Strata flake x86_64 only).

### 5.4 Permissions
sudo needs a password the agent cannot type (owner runs sudo). `ncu` counters blocked (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1). `jetson_clocks`/nvpmodel changes never run, so GPU clocks float (306-1020 MHz); mitigated with warm-up discard and counterbalanced A/B. Docker group, nvidia runtime config and apt installs were owner-authorized (D022).

### 5.5 Platform and memory
- Shared DRAM: no separate VRAM; NVML/nvidia-smi memory is [N/A]; per-client nvmap not visible; never sum `system-shared-dram` with process/cgroup scopes.
- cgroup/`--memory` cap does not bound CUDA allocations (D028); admission budget must say `guarantee: none-for-device-allocations`.
- llama.cpp auto-fit sizes context from "available memory", which on Tegra is system DRAM: unpinned `-c` picked n_ctx 45568 and 6568 MiB high-water (D023). Pin `-c`.
- `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` (+ `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES`) must be set explicitly for generic arm64 images; otherwise "CUDA driver version insufficient" (D022).
- `-lm auto` disables mmap on iGPU (llama-model.cpp:1590, ggml-cuda.cu:5473), so default over-memory runs die; baseline must say `-lm mmap`.
- Zram swap bursts trip naive swap-rate watchdogs (false positives at 33 and 286 MiB/s); limits settled at MemAvailable < 600 MiB, zram > 2.5 GiB, swap rate 1000 MiB/s (cmp sweep), two consecutive samples.
- Storage: 128 GB budget NVMe at ~570 MiB/s is a first-order design input; record drive model + fio matrix in every host inventory (D031).

### 5.6 Scheduling and logging
- One GPU job at a time; builds must not overlap timed runs (D029 unscored; D030/D031 contaminated by nice-19 replay).
- **pipeline4 deadlock**: the wait loop `while pgrep -f "python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py|...pipeline3.sh|...pipeline2.sh"` matched the launching shell's own command line (per the comment in pipeline5.sh), so the loop never ended. The GPU idled about 8.7 h (06:34 to 15:15 on 2026-11-10) and the kernel-screen stage never ran. Fix: wait on a PID (`while kill -0 <PID>`; pipeline6.sh does this); pipeline5.sh was rewritten without pgrep.
- Logging: run_op records intent/started/outcome with host_id; per-host evidence streams `evidence/jetson-arm/` (D021, host id from untracked ~/.config/siminfeng/host_id); run_op non-UTF-8 echo crash fixed (rc 0 reported as 1); telemetry JSONL ~3 MB per 3-minute trace run (bulk, not for git).
- Networking/transport: no SSH between hosts; exchange is git branches `jetson/*` pushed by the operator; evidence durability is sandbox-survivable only (host loss loses data). x86 has not answered round 2.

### 5.7 Recovery
Sandbox kill, runner SIGKILL, duplicate refusal, reconcile, retry-as-new-attempt all demonstrated on Jetson (3.x/2.3). Watchdog kill quoting bug (D029): `--kill-cmd "sg docker -c docker kill NAME"` was split by shlex so `docker` ran bare; fixed with single quotes and a live forced-trip test (watchdog-killtest). Exit codes must come from run_op records, not pipelines (D022: a `| tail` masked a status).

## 5. Lab Manager / CC portfolio discovery

### 5.1 Tools and commands used
bin/run_op (recorded commands; intent/started/outcome, survivors), bin/cc_hook, bin/lab (image add/submit/run/reconcile, host profiles + admission), bin/perf_summary, bin/ledger_appendix.py, cc/build_engine (target jetson-orin, ccache, `--extra-target`, `--with-tests`), cc/resource_observe (tegrastats/proc/cgroup/sysfs/io + watchdog), cc/om_run/om_run.sh (+ pipeline2-6, sweep_*.sh, build_queue.sh, fio_ceiling.sh), cc/expert_replay, cc/routing_trace (generic patch), cc/model_manifest/gguf_manifest.py, llama-bench / llama-perplexity (`--kl-divergence`, `-ub 1`) / llama-completion / llama-quantize, nsys (`--force-export=true` needed when a stale .sqlite gives a 0-byte CSV), tegrastats, fio, ccache 4.5.1, cmake/ninja from pip in ~/.local, docker + buildx, `codex exec` workers, git (`filter-branch` rescue, D024).

### 5.2 Missing tools and repeated manual work
- No "wait for job" primitive: every chain is a hand-written bash pipeline polling `pgrep -f` (pipeline2-6, build_queue). It broke once (5.6).
- Per-run summary extraction written as ad-hoc Python inline in pipelines (prompt/eval t/s from stderr, NVMe GiB and KiB/IO from telemetry, MemAvailable min, output sha) - candidate "run summarizer" CC.
- Flag capability probing: llama-bench lacks `-c`, `-cmoe`, `-mmp`; 11 attempts failed on flags (J-E003 x4, base-0435 x6, feas-b1 x1). Needs a `--help` capability probe before a queued run.
- Switch-effect verification: the NUMA switch was inert; only a log/counter line proved patch advice active. Need a standard "switch active" assertion per env-gated component.
- No A/A-aware acceptance gate in perf_summary yet (Strata autotune rule noted: median per-round ratio > max(3%, 2 x A/A gap, 2 x drift)).
- No launch identity record of the effective engine config (argv is recorded, effective config is not).
- Hand ordering of ABBA/ABAB arms and manual overlap avoidance with builds.
- Telemetry `host_id` field is the hostname (`satay`), not the campaign host id (`jetson-arm`) (D029; fix pending).
- Result classifier labels `watchdog_killed` while exit_code is 0 (feas-b1-a2).

### 5.3 Build and dependency problems
- System numpy is broken on Jetson; heavy converters run from `~/venvs/convert` (torch/transformers). Python tools stay stdlib.
- ccache first attempt had 0/454 hits because staging paths were random; fixed in J-T1b (CCACHE_BASEDIR, NOHASHDIR, compilercheck=content): rebuild 348/360 hits, 141 s vs 3154 s (D026). Binaries still differ per attempt (embedded `staging-...` path); `-ffile-prefix-map` not attempted.
- Docker installed by owner (docker.io 29.1.3, nvidia-ctk runtime); user is in group docker only for new sessions, so old sessions use `sg docker -c` (env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX='sg docker -c'`). buildx is a user plugin (v0.29.1).
- Host-built binaries have RUNPATH to deleted staging dirs, need `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; images need `--runtime nvidia` even for CPU tools.
- Each archive ~1.39 GB; disk 88 GB free at inventory, ~62 GB later with a 22 GB model.
- D024: `git add` of a directory a build was writing nearly published a 1.4 GB archive.
- Nix rejected (Strata flake x86_64 only).

### 5.4 Permissions
sudo needs a password the agent cannot type (owner runs sudo). `ncu` counters blocked (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1). `jetson_clocks`/nvpmodel changes never run, so GPU clocks float (306-1020 MHz); mitigated with warm-up discard and counterbalanced A/B. Docker group, nvidia runtime config and apt installs were owner-authorized (D022).

### 5.5 Platform and memory
- Shared DRAM: no separate VRAM; NVML/nvidia-smi memory is [N/A]; per-client nvmap not visible; never sum `system-shared-dram` with process/cgroup scopes.
- cgroup/`--memory` cap does not bound CUDA allocations (D028); admission budget must say `guarantee: none-for-device-allocations`.
- llama.cpp auto-fit sizes context from "available memory", which on Tegra is system DRAM: unpinned `-c` picked n_ctx 45568 and 6568 MiB high-water (D023). Pin `-c`.
- `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` (+ `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES`) must be set explicitly for generic arm64 images; otherwise "CUDA driver version insufficient" (D022).
- `-lm auto` disables mmap on iGPU (llama-model.cpp:1590, ggml-cuda.cu:5473), so default over-memory runs die; baseline must say `-lm mmap`.
- Zram swap bursts trip naive swap-rate watchdogs (false positives at 33 and 286 MiB/s); limits settled at MemAvailable < 600 MiB, zram > 2.5 GiB, swap rate 1000 MiB/s (cmp sweep), two consecutive samples.
- Storage: 128 GB budget NVMe at ~570 MiB/s is a first-order design input; record drive model + fio matrix in every host inventory (D031).

### 5.6 Scheduling and logging
- One GPU job at a time; builds must not overlap timed runs (D029 unscored; D030/D031 contaminated by nice-19 replay).
- **pipeline4 deadlock**: the wait loop `while pgrep -f "python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py|...pipeline3.sh|...pipeline2.sh"` matched the launching shell's own command line (per the comment in pipeline5.sh), so the loop never ended. The GPU idled about 8.7 h (06:34 to 15:15 on 2026-11-10) and the kernel-screen stage never ran. Fix: wait on a PID (`while kill -0 <PID>`; pipeline6.sh does this); pipeline5.sh was rewritten without pgrep.
- Logging: run_op records intent/started/outcome with host_id; per-host evidence streams `evidence/jetson-arm/` (D021, host id from untracked ~/.config/siminfeng/host_id); run_op non-UTF-8 echo crash fixed (rc 0 reported as 1); telemetry JSONL ~3 MB per 3-minute trace run (bulk, not for git).
- Networking/transport: no SSH between hosts; exchange is git branches `jetson/*` pushed by the operator; evidence durability is sandbox-survivable only (host loss loses data). x86 has not answered round 2.

### 5.7 Recovery
Sandbox kill, runner SIGKILL, duplicate refusal, reconcile, retry-as-new-attempt all demonstrated on Jetson (3.x/2.3). Watchdog kill quoting bug (D029): `--kill-cmd "sg docker -c docker kill NAME"` was split by shlex so `docker` ran bare; fixed with single quotes and a live forced-trip test (watchdog-killtest). Exit codes must come from run_op records, not pipelines (D022: a `| tail` masked a status).

Useful on discrete GPUs (x86 D044: +30..76% over static); a loss on UMA. `test-backend-ops perf` is the cheap screen (needs perf cases added, J-T6). Watch/adopt candidates from the external survey: #31957 (iGPU lazy-mode fallback only when mmap off), #31268/#30
- Strata (MIT, reference): replay policies (LFU-decay, adaptive swap), profile building from a varied corpus, `quant_quality` top-64 renormalised KL, autotune acceptance rule, benchmark protocol IDs, launch identity, management protocol patterns. Engine code does not transfer (own runtime).
- Candidate reuse for the 128 GB / 4 TB target: expert-sized aligned reads and router-informed exact prefetch are the mechanisms worth re-testing on a fast NVMe; the Jetson drive is IOPS-bound.

### Approaches to avoid (evidence-backed)
- `MADV_RANDOM` on the whole model file (D033: half speed).
- Static cross-workload hot sets (leave-one-out 16.6% vs LRU 62.4%).
- Cgroup/`--memory` caps as a GPU or shared-DRAM budget on Tegra (D028).
- `--numa distribute` on a 1-node host as a readahead switch (inert).
- Copying experts into a separate device bank on UMA (D030/D032).
- Treating hit rate as speed on unified memory, batch-512 ppl as a decode-kernel check, binary hash equality as "same build" (D026), raw t/s across hosts.
- Unfusing Q8_0 gate/up on Orin (-6.2%).
- `pgrep -f` wait loops launched from a shell whose command line contains the pattern.

### C. Component benchmarks and mechanism measurements
- C1 nsys kernel inventories (J-P001/2/3): mechanism for A1/A2 (fused MMVF 385 us vs 2 x MMF 131 us; Q4_K fused ~18 GB/s). Under profiling only.
- C2 NVMe ceiling (fio, D031): drive is 570 MiB/s class; 4 KiB qd1 19.6 MiB/s; PCIe Gen3 x4; one drive, read-only.
- C3 first-order model (D031): decode_tps ~ disk_BW / (615 MB x miss_rate); at 570 MiB/s and miss 1.0 -> ~1.0 t/s; measured 1.27-1.36 implies miss ~0.70-0.75. One model, a fit not a validation.

Slot-to-MiB mapping and prompt equivalence between trace and engine run were not audited here.

D032 shows the real cache did not cut NVMe reads (57-63 GiB in all arms), so that projection was NOT realized by the components tested; it remains an upper-bound estimate for a design not yet built.
- Caveats: one trace per workload (token counts not recorded in files I read); simulator assumes an expert-granular cache, the real system is a 4 KiB page cache; static-profile result is cross-workload only (leave-one-out), not same-workload.
- J-SPEC1 window-union replay: experiments/jetson/SPEC1/{SPEC1.md,results.json}; `expert_replay.py specwin` (Codex J-SPEC1; 14 tests + 5 subtests pass). 864 scenarios (4 workloads x W 1-8 x a 0.5/0.7/0.9 x LRU/Belady x 650/1300/2600 slots x optimistic/pessimistic). Best W>1 case 1.0011x (optimistic, LRU, code, 650 slots, a=0.9, W=2); a=0.7, W=4, LRU, 1300: 0.62-0.63x; all pessimistic cases slower. Reading: once a page/expert cache exists, consecutive-token expert overlap is already captured as hits at W=1, so verify batching adds no IO dedupe, while rejected drafts add misses. Simulation only; traces are natural text (no copy-heavy workload), so it does not cover n-gram on repeat text.

## 4. Predictions versus observations

Source: handoff/factory-ledger.html prediction register ("4 held, 7 missed or partial", of 11; hand-written at commit 6ae2616, before D031-D033), extended by predictions written in D029-D033 and assignments. Verdicts are mine from the cited files.

### 4.1 Ledger register (11)
| # | prediction | observed | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Jetson decode is launch-overhead bound | kernel bound, CUDA graphs already on (J-P001) | wrong |
| 2 | mmap doubles DRAM residency for a resident model | page cache reclaimable, no available-memory loss (J-E003) | wrong |
| 3 | kernel fusion is a win in general | depends on weight type and platform (D027: bf16/q4_K lose-fusion, q8_0 keeps) | partial (counted as a miss) |
| 4 | half the expert bytes (Q4_K) gives faster decode than Q8_0 | no until the dispatch fix; dequant bound | wrong |
| 5 | unfusing quantized gate/up keeps numerics identical | byte-identical ppl, KL and text (D027) | correct |
| 6 | a container memory limit caps GPU memory on Jetson | not charged to the cgroup (D028) | wrong |
| 7 | an expert cache with high hit rate speeds up decode | 64% hits, 17-23% slower on UMA (D030) | wrong |
| 8 | routing has exploitable locality | replay ~54% decode hits at ~12% capacity; 64% measured | correct |
| 9 | routing-frequency profile gives a good static hot set | leave-one-out 16.6% vs LRU 62% at 12.7% | wrong |
| 10 | llama.cpp default cannot load a model larger than RAM on Orin | confirmed from source and by the watchdog | correct |
| 11 | over-memory decode ~ NVMe bytes per token / fault-read bandwidth | ~1.3 t/s predicted, 1.26-1.37 measured (note: the model was partly fit to those runs, D031) | correct |

## 5. Lab Manager / CC portfolio discovery

### 5.1 Tools and commands used
bin/run_op (recorded commands; intent/started/outcome, survivors), bin/cc_hook, bin/lab (image add/submit/run/reconcile, host profiles + admission), bin/perf_summary, bin/ledger_appendix.py, cc/build_engine (target jetson-orin, ccache, `--extra-target`, `--with-tests`), cc/resource_observe (tegrastats/proc/cgroup/sysfs/io + watchdog), cc/om_run/om_run.sh (+ pipeline2-6, sweep_*.sh, build_queue.sh, fio_ceiling.sh), cc/expert_replay, cc/routing_trace (generic patch), cc/model_manifest/gguf_manifest.py, llama-bench / llama-perplexity (`--kl-divergence`, `-ub 1`) / llama-completion / llama-quantiz

### 5.2 Missing tools and repeated manual work
- No "wait for job" primitive: every chain is a hand-written bash pipeline polling `pgrep -f` (pipeline2-6, build_queue). It broke once (5.6).
- Per-run summary extraction written as ad-hoc Python inline in pipelines (prompt/eval t/s from stderr, NVMe GiB and KiB/IO from telemetry, MemAvailable min, output sha) - candidate "run summarizer" CC.
- Flag capability probing: llama-bench lacks `-c`, `-cmoe`, `-mmp`; 11 attempts failed on flags (J-E003 x4, base-0435 x6, feas-b1 x1). Needs a `--help` capability probe before a queued run.
- Switch-effect verification: the NUMA switch was inert; only a log/counter line proved patch advice active. Need a standard "switch active" assertion per env-gated component.
- No A/A-aware acceptance gate in perf_summary yet (Strata autotune rule noted: median per-round ratio > max(3%, 2 x A/A gap, 2 x drift)).
- No launch identity record of the effective engine config (argv is recorded, effective config is not).
- Hand ordering of ABBA/ABAB arms and manual overlap avoidance with builds.
- Telemetry `host_id` field is the hostname (`satay`), not the campaign host id (`jetson-arm`) (D029; fix pending).
- Result classifier labels `watchdog_killed` while exit_code is 0 (feas-b1-a2).

### 5.3 Build and dependency problems
- System numpy is broken on Jetson; heavy converters run from `~/venvs/convert` (torch/transformers). Python tools stay stdlib.
- ccache first attempt had 0/454 hits because staging paths were random; fixed in J-T1b (CCACHE_BASEDIR, NOHASHDIR, compilercheck=content): rebuild 348/360 hits, 141 s vs 3154 s (D026). Binaries still differ per attempt (embedded `staging-...` path); `-ffile-prefix-map` not attempted.
- Docker installed by owner (docker.io 29.1.3, nvidia-ctk runtime); user is in group docker only for new sessions, so old sessions use `sg docker -c` (env `DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX='sg docker -c'`). buildx is a user plugin (v0.29.1).
- Host-built binaries have RUNPATH to deleted staging dirs, need `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; images need `--runtime nvidia` even for CPU tools.
- Each archive ~1.39 GB; disk 88 GB free at inventory, ~62 GB later with a 22 GB model.
- D024: `git add` of a directory a build was writing nearly published a 1.4 GB archive.
- Nix rejected (Strata flake x86_64 only).

### 5.4 Permissions
sudo needs a password the agent cannot type (owner runs sudo). `ncu` counters blocked (RmProfilingAdminOnly=1). `jetson_clocks`/nvpmodel changes never run, so GPU clocks float (306-1020 MHz); mitigated with warm-up discard and counterbalanced A/B. Docker group, nvidia runtime config and apt installs were owner-authorized (D022).

### 5.5 Platform and memory
- Shared DRAM: no separate VRAM; NVML/nvidia-smi memory is [N/A]; per-client nvmap not visible; never sum `system-shared-dram` with process/cgroup scopes.
- cgroup/`--memory` cap does not bound CUDA allocations (D028); admission budget must say `guarantee: none-for-device-allocations`.
- llama.cpp auto-fit sizes context from "available memory", which on Tegra is system DRAM: unpinned `-c` picked n_ctx 45568 and 6568 MiB high-water (D023). Pin `-c`.
- `NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all` (+ `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES`) must be set explicitly for generic arm64 images; otherwise "CUDA driver version insufficient" (D022).
- `-lm auto` disables mmap on iGPU (llama-model.cpp:1590, ggml-cuda.cu:5473), so default over-memory runs die; baseline must say `-lm mmap`.
- Zram swap bursts trip naive swap-rate watchdogs (false positives at 33 and 286 MiB/s); limits settled at MemAvailable < 600 MiB, zram > 2.5 GiB, swap rate 1000 MiB/s (cmp sweep), two consecutive samples.
- Storage: 128 GB budget NVMe at ~570 MiB/s is a first-order design input; record drive model + fio matrix in every host inventory (D031).

### 5.6 Scheduling and logging
- One GPU job at a time; builds must not overlap timed runs (D029 unscored; D030/D031 contaminated by nice-19 replay).
- **pipeline4 deadlock**: the wait loop `while pgrep -f "python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py|...pipeline3.sh|...pipeline2.sh"` matched the launching shell's own command line (per the comment in pipeline5.sh), so the loop never ended. The GPU idled about 8.7 h (06:34 to 15:15 on 2026-11-10) and the kernel-screen stage never ran. Fix: wait on a PID (`while kill -0 <PID>`; pipeline6.sh does this); pipeline5.sh was rewritten without pgrep.
- Logging: run_op records intent/started/outcome with host_id; per-host evidence streams `evidence/jetson-arm/` (D021, host id from untracked ~/.config/siminfeng/host_id); run_op non-UTF-8 echo crash fixed (rc 0 reported as 1); telemetry JSONL ~3 MB per 3-minute trace run (bulk, not for git).
- Networking/transport: no SSH between hosts; exchange is git branches `jetson/*` pushed by the operator; evidence durability is sandbox-survivable only (host loss loses data). x86 has not answered round 2.

### 5.7 Recovery
Sandbox kill, runner SIGKILL, duplicate refusal, reconcile, retry-as-new-attempt all demonstrated on Jetson (3.x/2.3). Watchdog kill quoting bug (D029): `--kill-cmd "sg docker -c docker kill NAME"` was split by shlex so `docker` ran bare; fixed with single quotes and a live forced-trip test (watchdog-killtest). Exit codes must come from run_op records, not pipelines (D022: a `| tail` masked a status).

### Upstream and external reuse
- llama.cpp: `--moe-cache-mib` (#29887), CPU-share (#30966), ClassLRU (#31233), CPU does not wait on cached experts (#31888, in cf34d311). Useful on discrete GPUs (x86 D044: +30..76% over static); a loss on UMA. `test-backend-ops perf` is the cheap screen (needs perf cases added, J-T6). Watch/adopt candidates from the external survey: #31957 (iGPU lazy-mode fallback only when mmap off), #31268/#30858/#28285 (Orin MMVQ), #31469 (study only, qwen4exp-only).
- Strata (MIT, reference): replay policies (LFU-decay, adaptive swap), profile building from a varied corpus, `quant_quality` top-64 renormalised KL, autotune acceptance rule, benchmark protocol IDs, launch identity, management protocol patterns. Engine code does not transfer (own runtime).
- Candidate reuse for the 128 GB / 4 TB target: expert-sized aligned reads and router-informed exact prefetch are the mechanisms worth re-testing on a fast NVMe; the Jetson drive is IOPS-bound.

### Approaches to avoid (evidence-backed)
- `MADV_RANDOM` on the whole model file (D033: half speed).
- Static cross-workload hot sets (leave-one-out 16.6% vs LRU 62.4%).
- Cgroup/`--memory` caps as a GPU or shared-DRAM budget on Tegra (D028).
- `--numa distribute` on a 1-node host as a readahead switch (inert).
- Copying experts into a separate device bank on UMA (D030/D032).
- Treating hit rate as speed on unified memory, batch-512 ppl as a decode-kernel check, binary hash equality as "same build" (D026), raw t/s across hosts.
- Unfusing Q8_0 gate/up on Orin (-6.2%).
- `pgrep -f`/`pkill -f` patterns launched from a shell whose command line contains the pattern (pipeline4 deadlocked ~8.7 h; a closeout `pkill -f` also killed its own shell).

### Code and Commit Standards

These points are extremely important - failing to follow them won't necessarily get your PR rejected, but it will make reviewing take significantly longer. Please follow them carefully:

- Avoid emdash `—`, unicode arrow `→` or any unicode characters: `×`, `…` ; use ASCII equivalents instead: `-`, `->`, `x`, `...`
- Code comments:
    - Keep code comments concise (usually 1-2 lines)
    - Avoid redundant or excessive inline commentary
    - Avoid hard-wrapping it to a fixed column width - that hurts readability
    - Use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, simple wordings (write like cavemen if needed)
    - Note: Remind yourself of this point regularly, as it often gets lost between context compactions
- Prefer reusing existing infrastructure over introducing new components. Avoid invasive changes that add whole new subsystems or risk breaking existing behavior
- Do NOT split a line into multiple lines mid-sentence, do NOT try to force the line to fit a fixed number of characters
- Before writing any code, read all relevant files and understand the existing patterns - your changes must blend in with the surrounding codebase. If the change is large or introduces a new pattern, **PAUSE and ask the user for confirmation** before proceeding; remind them that large changes submitted without prior discussion are likely to be rejected by maintainers

Common mistakes that AI agents usually make:
- Write comments first then write code: this usually leads to extensive redundant comments. Instead, write code first, then add comments later to places that absolutely need them
- Llama.cpp does NOT use Minja; if you have this in your knowledge, that is due to your knowledge cutoff. Llama.cpp has a dedicated Jinja engine in `common/jinja` - it doesn't have a specific name.

Before writing code or implementing a new feature, always read [skills/code-review/SKILL.md](skills/code-review/SKILL.md). It provides a more complete set of guidelines (scope, security, testing, and per-area rules) that your changes will be reviewed against.

### Prohibited Actions

- Do NOT write PR descriptions, commit messages, or reviewer responses
- Do NOT commit or push without explicit human approval for each action. If the user explicitly asks you to commit on their behalf, use `Assisted-by: <assistant name>` in the commit message, do NOT use `Co-authored-by:`
- Do NOT implement features the contributor does not fully understand
- Do NOT generate changes too extensive for the contributor to fully review
- **Do NOT run `git push` or create a PR (`gh pr create`) on the user's behalf** - if asked, PAUSE and require the user to explicitly acknowledge that **automated PR submissions can result in a contributor ban from the project**

When uncertain, err toward minimal assistance.

User: Please create and submit the PR for me.
Agent: I'm sorry, I cannot submit the PR for you. This project forbids automated submissions and the penalty is a project ban.

User: Please address the reviewer comments.
Agent: I'm sorry, I cannot reply to the reviewers. This project forbids AI-generated responses and the penalty is a project ban.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""om_spec.py - guarded over-memory n-gram self-speculation probe on jetson-arm (adapted from x86 artifacts/spec1/probe2.py).
Starts llama-server in a campaign-labelled container (Qwen3.6-35B over-memory, -lm mmap -ngl 99 -cmoe), runs the same
watchdog as om_run.sh, sends 3 prompts (rewrite/repeat copy-heavy, chat), records timings + draft acceptance + text hash + IO.
usage: om_spec.py OUTDIR IMAGE CFG [ROUND]   CFG in base|ngram-mod"""
import json, subprocess, sys, time, urllib.request, hashlib, os, signal
OUT, IMG, CFG = sys.argv[1:4]; RND = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else "1"
R = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../.."))
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)
MD = os.path.expanduser("~/models/campaign/qwen36-35b-a3b")
code = open(R + "/artifacts/traces/in/code.txt").read(); chat = open(R + "/artifacts/traces/in/chat.txt").read()
PROMPTS = {"rewrite": "/no_think Rewrite the following code exactly, but rename the variable `i` to `idx` everywhere. Output only code.\n\n" + code[:1500] + "\n\nRewritten code:\n",
           "repeat": "/no_think Repeat this list exactly once more:\n" + "\n".join(f"item {i}: value={i*7%13}" for i in range(40)) + "\n\nRepeated list:\n",
           "chat": chat}
EXTRA = {"base": [], "ngram-mod": ["--spec-type", "ngram-mod"]}[CFG]
NAME = f"omspec-{int(time.time())}"
def dk(cmd): return subprocess.run(["sg", "docker", "-c", "docker " + cmd], capture_output=True, text=True)
def devstat():
    for l in open("/sys/class/block/nvme0n1/stat"): f = l.split(); return int(f[0]), int(f[2])
args = " ".join(["-m /om/model.gguf -ngl 99 -cmoe -lm mmap -c 4096 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 -np 1"] + EXTRA)
r = dk(f"run -d --name {NAME} --runtime nvidia --label campaign=c1 --label om=1 -p 127.0.0.1:18080:8080 -v {MD}:/om:ro --entrypoint /app/llama-server {IMG} {args}")
if r.returncode: print("START_FAIL", r.stderr); sys.exit(2)
wd = subprocess.Popen(["python3", R + "/cc/resource_observe/resource_observe.py", "watchdog", "--min-available-mib", "600", "--max-swap-used-mib", "2560",
                       "--max-swap-rate-mibs", "1000", "--interval-ms", "250", "--kill-cmd", f"sg docker -c 'docker kill {NAME}'", "--out", OUT + "/watchdog.jsonl"])
sm = subprocess.Popen(["python3", R + "/cc/resource_observe/resource_observe.py", "sample", "--backends", "io,proc,tegrastats", "--path", MD,
                       "--interval-ms", "1000", "--duration-s", "5400", "--out", OUT + "/telemetry.jsonl"], stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
recs = []; status = "ok"
try:
    t0 = time.time()
    while True:
        try:
            if urllib.request.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:18080/health", timeout=2).status == 200: break
        except Exception: pass
        if time.time() - t0 > 900 or NAME not in dk("ps --filter name=" + NAME + " --format '{{.Names}}'").stdout: raise SystemExit("server not ready")
        time.sleep(2)
    load_s = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
    for pn, p in PROMPTS.items():
        a = devstat(); ts = time.time()
        body = json.dumps({"prompt": p, "n_predict": 96, "temperature": 0, "seed": 1, "cache_prompt": False}).encode()
        resp = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:18080/completion", body, {"Content-Type": "application/json"}), timeout=1800))
        b = devstat(); t = resp.get("timings", {})
        rec = dict(round=RND, cfg=CFG, prompt=pn, load_s=load_s, wall_s=round(time.time() - ts, 1), tps=t.get("predicted_per_second"), pp_tps=t.get("prompt_per_second"),
                   prompt_n=t.get("prompt_n"), n=t.get("predicted_n"), draft_n=t.get("draft_n"), draft_acc=t.get("draft_n_accepted"),
                   nvme_gib=round((b[1] - a[1]) * 512 / 2**30, 2), avg_kib_io=round((b[1] - a[1]) * 0.5 / max(b[0] - a[0], 1)),
                   text_sha=hashlib.sha256(resp["content"].encode()).hexdigest()[:12], head=resp["content"][:60])
        print(json.dumps(rec), flush=True); recs.append(rec)
except BaseException as e:
    status = "failed: " + repr(e)[:300]
finally:
    lg = dk("logs " + NAME); open(OUT + "/server.log", "w").write(lg.stdout + lg.stderr)
    dk("rm -f " + NAME); wd.terminate(); sm.terminate()
    trips = sum(1 for l in open(OUT + "/watchdog.jsonl") if "watchdog_trip" in l) if os.path.exists(OUT + "/watchdog.jsonl") else 0
    json.dump(dict(image=IMG, cfg=CFG, round=RND, status="watchdog_killed" if trips else status, records=recs), open(OUT + "/result.json", "w"), indent=1)
    print("STATUS", status, "trips", trips)

# Assignment H2 — declarative A/B runner + run summarizer + acceptance gate + preflight (harness; host jetson-arm; worker Codex)
Repo root: /home/muk/projects/siminfeng/campaign. Read first: CLOSEOUT.md 5.2, 6 (methodology rows), 2.4; cc/om_run/om_run.sh (outdir layout: cmd.txt result.json stdout.txt stderr.txt telemetry.jsonl watchdog.jsonl); cc/om_run/pipeline5.sh (the inline summarizer you are replacing); experiments/jetson/OM/om7-20261110-1555/* (real fixture data: 6 arms base/pf/pfn); experiments/jetson/J-E007-unfuse-by-type/*.json (llama-bench JSON fixture); bin/perf_summary.
Problem: every experiment re-implements ordering, metric extraction and verdicts in ad-hoc bash/Python; 11 runs died on nonexistent flags; one "switch" was silently inert (numa); no A/A-aware gate.

## Deliverables (python3 stdlib only; package dir cc/abrun/)
1. `cc/abrun/run_summary.py DIR [DIR...] [--json]` -> per run dir a summary dict, also written to DIR/summary.json:
   status (from result.json), wall_s, prompt_tps / eval_tps (last `common_perf_print` prompt eval / eval lines in stderr; also llama-bench `-o json` stdout: pp/tg avg_ts and samples_ts, steady = mean of samples[1:]), load_s, nvme_gib (max-min of telemetry metric `device_read`, KiB units), avg_kib_per_io (device_read delta / device_read_ios delta), nvme_gib_per_token (when eval tokens parsed), mem_available_min_mib, swap max, gpu_freq median, output_sha (sha256 of stdout.txt, first 12 hex), and `switch_lines`: stderr lines matching any regex given via `--switch-regex`. Missing metrics -> null + reason string, never crash.
2. `cc/abrun/gate.py`: given labelled summaries (arm -> list of runs, in execution order) compute per-arm mean of the chosen metric, the B/A ratio, A/A gap (if an arm has >= 2 runs: (max-min)/mean of that arm; take the max over arms), drift (first-half vs second-half of the base arm), and verdict per the rule: `improved` if ratio-1 > max(0.03, 2*aa_gap, 2*drift); `regressed` if 1-ratio > same threshold; else `null`. Also an output-class check: `identical` (all output_sha equal across arms), `differs` (list which). Verdict object is JSON, includes every input number.
3. `cc/abrun/preflight.py`: given image + tool + argv, obtain `/app/TOOL --help` text (via a pluggable runner; real runner = `$DOCKER_CMD_PREFIX docker run --rm --runtime nvidia --entrypoint /app/TOOL IMAGE --help`, cached under lab/preflight/<sha of image ref + tool>.txt) and reject any `-x`/`--xx` flag in argv not present in the help text. Exit nonzero with the offending flags listed.
4. `cc/abrun/abrun.py SPEC.json [--dry-run] [--submit]`: spec schema (document it in README):

# Local job queue

Run from the campaign root. Python 3 standard library only; jobs use `bin/run_op`
with agent `jobq` and the submitted name as task. No worker starts automatically.

```sh
build=$(bin/jobq submit --class build --name engine --timeout 7200 -- python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py ...)
run=$(bin/jobq submit --class gpu --after "$build" --name timing --timeout 5400 -- python3 cc/om_spec/om_spec.py ...)
bin/jobq worker --once
bin/jobq wait "$run" --timeout 600
bin/jobq list
bin/jobq show "$run"
bin/jobq cancel "$run"
```

`worker` polls continuously; `worker --once` drains the queue until idle, including
jobs made ready by dependencies. Multiple workers share the same admission lock.
Eligible jobs are admitted FIFO; blocked jobs do not prevent compatible work.
A failed, cancelled, timed out, or skipped dependency causes `skipped_dep_failed`.
`wait` returns 0 for success, 1 for any other terminal state, 2 for wait timeout.
Wait timeout does not cancel work. Job timeout terminates its process groups.
Cancellation sends TERM, then KILL after a short grace period if needed.

At most one GPU or build job runs at once. CPU jobs can overlap builds; CPU jobs
exclude GPU jobs unless submitted with `--allow-during-gpu`. This prevents the
build/timing contamination seen in D029/D031. The rule works in both directions.
Only commands admitted through this queue are covered by its exclusivity rules.

State defaults to `lab/jobq/`: one JSON per job, append-only `events.jsonl`, a
`lock`, and per-job logs. JSON records command PID/group, wrapper group, times,
exit status, dependencies, and symmetric `concurrent_jobs` overlap history.
A worker restart detects a dead job supervisor and fails the abandoned job.
`JOBQ_DIR` overrides state storage; `JOBQ_RUN_OP` selects a test wrapper.
Submit preserves the working directory and environment for execution.

Migration of `cc/om_run/pipeline6.sh` (run after the preceding pipeline's job):

```sh
O=experiments/jetson/SPEC2-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M)
IMG=campaign/llamacpp:jetson-up1108
prev=$pipeline5_job_id
for arm in 'base 1' 'ngram-mod 1' 'ngram-mod 2' 'base 2'; do
  set -- $arm
  prev=$(bin/jobq submit --class gpu --after "$prev" \
    --name "J-SPEC2-$1-r$2" --timeout 5400 -- \
    python3 cc/om_spec/om_spec.py "$O/$1-r$2" "$IMG" "$1" "$2")
done
bin/jobq worker --once
bin/jobq wait "$prev"
```

Run from the campaign root. Python 3 standard library only; jobs use `bin/run_op`
with agent `jobq` and the submitted name as task. No worker starts automatically.

```sh
build=$(bin/jobq submit --class build --name engine --timeout 7200 -- python3 cc/build_engine/build_engine.py ...)
run=$(bin/jobq submit --class gpu --after "$build" --name timing --timeout 5400 -- python3 cc/om_spec/om_spec.py ...)
bin/jobq worker --once
bin/jobq wait "$run" --timeout 600
bin/jobq list
bin/jobq show "$run"
bin/jobq cancel "$run"
```

`worker` polls continuously; `worker --once` drains the queue until idle, including
jobs made ready by dependencies. Multiple workers share the same admission lock.
Eligible jobs are admitted FIFO; blocked jobs do not prevent compatible work.
A failed, cancelled, timed out, or skipped dependency causes `skipped_dep_failed`.
`wait` returns 0 for success, 1 for any other terminal state, 2 for wait timeout.
Wait timeout does not cancel work. Job timeout terminates its process groups.
Cancellation sends TERM, then KILL after a short grace period if needed.

Repo root: /home/muk/projects/siminfeng/campaign. Builds on 01-05 (cc/mmap_advice/patches/combined-01-02-03-04-05.patch; cc/expert_fill/expert_fill.h single source of truth). Engine tree ref/llama.cpp-up1108 @ cf34d311 — never modify in place; work in /tmp copy.

Faults are minor (162 majflt/token). J-OM7 (CLOSEOUT 2.4 om7 row) showed naive next-layer prediction (reuse layer L ids for L+1) has 3% precision. Hypothesis: predicting layer L+1's experts by applying layer L+1's router to layer L's MoE input (pre-gating; known from MoE offloading literature to give high next-layer recall) gives enough lead time to overlap most fill IO with compute.
## Design (verify each assumption in the code; state where it is false)
- At the existing CPU observer hook for layer L's expert MUL_MAT_ID (patch 02/05), under `-cmoe` the MoE input activations for layer L are on host (src1 of the CPU MUL_MAT_ID, or the tensor feeding it). Read it (decode ubatch only, n_tokens == 1).

# Assignment J-OM10b — fix pre-gate prefetch scheduling (component rework; worker Codex)
Repo root: /home/muk/projects/siminfeng/campaign. Builds on 01-06 (cc/mmap_advice/patches/combined-01-02-03-04-05-06.patch, cc/expert_fill/expert_fill.h single source). Engine tree ref/llama.cpp-up1108 @ cf34d311, never modify in place.
## Evidence (experiments/jetson/OM/J-OM10: REPORT.md, `expert_pregate: stats` in */stderr.txt)
Predictor works: recall@8 0.81. But decode pg8 1.23 vs frd16 (no prefetch) 1.29 t/s; pg16 0.75. pg8 run: async_bytes_read 10.3 GB + sync 3.4 GB (frd16 reads ~10.5 GB total) → ~30% more IO; pending_reads 3725, inflight_at_arrival 571.
Lead's diagnosis from 06-pregate.patch (verify, then fix):
 (a) In the CPU observer path, `expert_pregate_hook(il, ...)` (prefetch for L+1) is called BEFORE `expert_fill_selected(il, ...)` (demand fill for L) → prefetch reads compete with the demand fill on the drive and on the workers.
 (b) When layer L+1 arrives, async jobs for L+1 that have NOT started are still queued; the sync fill reads the same non-resident pages, and the stale async jobs later read them again (or evict useful pages).
 (c) Async jobs may occupy all fill workers, delaying demand jobs that arrive while they run.
## Deliverables

# Measurement gaps — what we could not measure, or measured badly (2026-11-11)

Sources: CLOSEOUT.md §5/§7 + Addendum c2, c2/SHAPE.md, D034–D036, J-OM10c run dirs (summary.json, telemetry.jsonl, stderr.txt).
Severity: **H** = can change a conclusion; M = limits interpretation; L = bookkeeping.

## 1. Collected but never reported (cheap fixes; data already on disk)
| Gap | Evidence | Sev | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu_freq_median` is null in **56/56** abrun summaries | summary.json `reasons` lists it every run; tegrastats on this L4T gives GR3D % only | M | read `/sys/class/devfreq/*gpu*/cur_freq` in resource_observe |
| GPU utilisation sampled but not summarised | J-OM10c/003 telemetry: gpu_util median 4 %, max 99 % → decode is IO-bound, GPU idle | M | add gpu_util median/p90 to summary + secondary table |
| Power sampled but no energy metric | VDD_IN median ~6.06 W; no J/token anywhere | M | J/token = ∫VDD_IN over eval window / tokens |
| NVMe busy (`device_util`, io_ticks) not summarised | collected per 0.5 s sample | M | add device_util during eval window |
| t/s printed to 2 decimals and used by the gate | `1.40 tokens per second` vs `716.54 ms per token`; at 1.4 t/s one step = 0.7 %, a third of the A/A gap | **H** for close arms | gate on ms/token (eval_ms / runs) instead of rounded t/s |

## 2. Window/resolution problems
| Gap | Evidence | Sev |
|---|---|---|
| NVMe GiB/token divides whole-run bytes (load + prefill + decode) by decode tokens | load 60 s of ~145 s wall (J-OM10c/003 stderr) | **H** for IO conclusions — need per-phase byte split using eval timestamps |
| Telemetry is 0.5 s sampling vs ~715 ms/token | tegrastats dt median 0.50 s | M — cannot see per-token phases (fill vs compute vs idle) |
| vmstat / block counters are system-wide | include docker, codex, other procs | M — fine under jobq exclusivity, not otherwise |
| Peak MiB/s values are sampling artefacts | 825 MiB/s > drive ceiling 570 (D031) | L |
| Per-token time breakdown exists only with the diag patch (J-OM9), which costs ~9 % | D034 | M — need a cheap always-on counter (ns in fill wait per token) |

## 3. Prefetch internals we cannot see (blocks next tuning step)
- **Timeliness**: `hits` counts correct predictions, not "page resident before demand". `async_wait_ns_in_demand` was omitted in 07. We do not know how many of the 81 % correct predictions actually arrived in time. **H** — this is the metric that decides K, inflight and L+2.
- Wasted IO: cancelled_bytes is counted (4.35 GB in pg8b), but bytes read async and then evicted before use are not counted.
- Drive queue depth / latency distribution: no iostat/blktrace (no sudo); only avg KiB/IO.
- Fill bandwidth ~380 MB/s vs drive 570 MiB/s: the cause of the gap (syscall size, QD, page-cache insertion cost) is unmeasured.

## 4. Config verification (the switch is on, but is it the value you asked for?)
- **J-OM10c pg10i8 requested K=10 but ran K=8** (parser accepts only 12/16, silently falls back). The switch regex proved "pregate active", not "k=10". Same class as earlier: `--numa` inert (D032), direct-fill never activated (D032), OR-regex in J-OM8b. **H** — arm names are not trustworthy.
- Fix: every env-gated component logs one `effective config` line with all parsed values; abrun asserts each arm's expected values (not just a regex on "active"); unknown/invalid values → hard fail, not fallback.

## 5. Things we cannot measure on this host / with these permissions
| Gap | Cause | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| GPU kernel counters (ncu) | RmProfilingAdminOnly=1 | no kernel-level attribution on Orin |
| CPU profiles (perf) | not installed, paranoid=2, no sudo | CPU-side fill/syscall cost unprofiled |
| Fixed clocks | jetson_clocks/nvpmodel not run (no sudo) | GPU 306–1020 MHz floats; mitigated by counterbalancing only |
| Cold-cache control | no `drop_caches` (no sudo); grep finds none in abrun/om_run | page-cache state at run start uncontrolled (partly self-flushing since 20.8 GiB > 7.4 GiB RAM) |
| Target scale (≈500 GB on 128 GB) | host is 7.4 GiB + 128 GB drive | proxy ratio 2.8× vs target ~3.9×; no validated extrapolation; one drive model |

## 6. Statistical / workload coverage
- n = 2 runs per arm (4 in J-OM8b); A/A 1.6–2.6 %, gate threshold ~4–5 %. Gate compares arms to base only. **Neighbouring arms (pg8b/pg8i8/pg8i12/"pg10i8": 1.37–1.40) are indistinguishable** — no occupancy conclusion is possible.
- One prompt, 64 decode tokens, greedy, batch 1, `-c 4096`. No TTFT, long-context, multi-turn, batch >1, or chat-template workloads (SPEC2 chat arm invalid). Routing (and so prefetch recall) is workload-dependent (replay: LRU 0.54–0.69 by workload).
- Prefill run-to-run spread is large (4.92–5.73 t/s inside one arm in J-OM10c); prefill is not gated.
- Quality = output-hash identity on 64 tokens only (fine for lossless IO changes; not enough for any lossy change).

## 7. Bookkeeping / provenance
- Model checksums: Qwen sha not re-verified locally; Granite safetensors and KL base sha not recorded on Jetson.
- Trace token counts not recorded; replay ↔ engine slot/MiB mapping not audited.
- SHAPE: "GPU busy" = command lifetime, not utilisation; 19 failures classified `other`; Haiku check-in tokens/cost not tracked (only Codex).
- x86 cross-host transfer (sm_120 for D025/D027) still unanswered.

## Priority fix list (proposed H5 / J-OM11)
1. Gate on ms/token; per-phase NVMe bytes (decode window only). — harness, cheap
2. Summarise gpu_util, device_util, J/token, GPU freq from sysfs. — harness, cheap
3. Effective-config log line + per-arm value assertions; invalid env → fail. — engine + abrun
4. Prefetch timeliness counters: prefetched-and-resident-at-demand, demand wait ns per token, async bytes evicted unused. — engine
5. Workload matrix (≥3 prompts incl. chat template, 256 tokens) and n ≥ 3 for arms < 5 % apart. — spec

# Measurement gaps — what we could not measure, or measured badly (2026-11-11)

Sources: CLOSEOUT.md §5/§7 + Addendum c2, c2/SHAPE.md, D034–D036, J-OM10c run dirs (summary.json, telemetry.jsonl, stderr.txt).
Severity: **H** = can change a conclusion; M = limits interpretation; L = bookkeeping.

## 1. Collected but never reported (cheap fixes; data already on disk)
| Gap | Evidence | Sev | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gpu_freq_median` is null in **56/56** abrun summaries | summary.json `reasons` lists it every run; tegrastats on this L4T gives GR3D % only | M | read `/sys/class/devfreq/*gpu*/cur_freq` in resource_observe |
| GPU utilisation sampled but not summarised | J-OM10c/003 telemetry: gpu_util median 4 %, max 99 % → decode is IO-bound, GPU idle | M | add gpu_util median/p90 to summary + secondary table |
| Power sampled but no energy metric | VDD_IN median ~6.06 W; no J/token anywhere | M | J/token = ∫VDD_IN over eval window / tokens |
| NVMe busy (`device_util`, io_ticks) not summarised | collected per 0.5 s sample | M | add device_util during eval window |
| t/s printed to 2 decimals and used by the gate | `1.40 tokens per second` vs `716.54 ms per token`; at 1.4 t/s one step = 0.7 %, a third of the A/A gap | **H** for close arms | gate on ms/token (eval_ms / runs) instead of rounded t/s |

## 2. Window/resolution problems
| Gap | Evidence | Sev |
|---|---|---|
| NVMe GiB/token divides whole-run bytes (load + prefill + decode) by decode tokens | load 60 s of ~145 s wall (J-OM10c/003 stderr) | **H** for IO conclusions — need per-phase byte split using eval timestamps |
| Telemetry is 0.5 s sampling vs ~715 ms/token | tegrastats dt median 0.50 s | M — cannot see per-token phases (fill vs compute vs idle) |
| vmstat / block counters are system-wide | include docker, codex, other procs | M — fine under jobq exclusivity, not otherwise |
| Peak MiB/s values are sampling artefacts | 825 MiB/s > drive ceiling 570 (D031) | L |
| Per-token time breakdown exists only with the diag patch (J-OM9), which costs ~9 % | D034 | M — need a cheap always-on counter (ns in fill wait per token) |

## 3. Prefetch internals we cannot see (blocks next tuning step)
- **Timeliness**: `hits` counts correct predictions, not "page resident before demand". `async_wait_ns_in_demand` was omitted in 07. We do not know how many of the 81 % correct predictions actually arrived in time. **H** — this is the metric that decides K, inflight and L+2.
- Wasted IO: cancelled_bytes is counted (4.35 GB in pg8b), but bytes read async and then evicted before use are not counted.
- Drive queue depth / latency distribution: no iostat/blktrace (no sudo); only avg KiB/IO.
- Fill bandwidth ~380 MB/s vs drive 570 MiB/s: the cause of the gap (syscall size, QD, page-cache insertion cost) is unmeasured.

## 4. Config verification (the switch is on, but is it the value you asked for?)
- **J-OM10c pg10i8 requested K=10 but ran K=8** (parser accepts only 12/16, silently falls back). The switch regex proved "pregate active", not "k=10". Same class as earlier: `--numa` inert (D032), direct-fill never activated (D032), OR-regex in J-OM8b. **H** — arm names are not trustworthy.
- Fix: every env-gated component logs one `effective config` line with all parsed values; abrun asserts each arm's expected values (not just a regex on "active"); unknown/invalid values → hard fail, not fallback.

## 5. Things we cannot measure on this host / with these permissions
| Gap | Cause | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| GPU kernel counters (ncu) | RmProfilingAdminOnly=1 | no kernel-level attribution on Orin |
| CPU profiles (perf) | not installed, paranoid=2, no sudo | CPU-side fill/syscall cost unprofiled |
| Fixed clocks | jetson_clocks/nvpmodel not run (no sudo) | GPU 306–1020 MHz floats; mitigated by counterbalancing only |
| Cold-cache control | no `drop_caches` (no sudo); grep finds none in abrun/om_run | page-cache state at run start uncontrolled (partly self-flushing since 20.8 GiB > 7.4 GiB RAM) |
| Target scale (≈500 GB on 128 GB) | host is 7.4 GiB + 128 GB drive | proxy ratio 2.8× vs target ~3.9×; no validated extrapolation; one drive model |

## 6. Statistical / workload coverage
- n = 2 runs per arm (4 in J-OM8b); A/A 1.6–2.6 %, gate threshold ~4–5 %. Gate compares arms to base only. **Neighbouring arms (pg8b/pg8i8/pg8i12/"pg10i8": 1.37–1.40) are indistinguishable** — no occupancy conclusion is possible.
- One prompt, 64 decode tokens, greedy, batch 1, `-c 4096`. No TTFT, long-context, multi-turn, batch >1, or chat-template workloads (SPEC2 chat arm invalid). Routing (and so prefetch recall) is workload-dependent (replay: LRU 0.54–0.69 by workload).
- Prefill run-to-run spread is large (4.92–5.73 t/s inside one arm in J-OM10c); prefill is not gated.
- Quality = output-hash identity on 64 tokens only (fine for lossless IO changes; not enough for any lossy change).

## 7. Bookkeeping / provenance
- Model checksums: Qwen sha not re-verified locally; Granite safetensors and KL base sha not recorded on Jetson.
- Trace token counts not recorded; replay ↔ engine slot/MiB mapping not audited.
- SHAPE: "GPU busy" = command lifetime, not utilisation; 19 failures classified `other`; Haiku check-in tokens/cost not tracked (only Codex).
- x86 cross-host transfer (sm_120 for D025/D027) still unanswered.

## Priority fix list (proposed H5 / J-OM11)
1. Gate on ms/token; per-phase NVMe bytes (decode window only). — harness, cheap
2. Summarise gpu_util, device_util, J/token, GPU freq from sysfs. — harness, cheap
3. Effective-config log line + per-arm value assertions; invalid env → fail. — engine + abrun
4. Prefetch timeliness counters: prefetched-and-resident-at-demand, demand wait ns per token, async bytes evicted unused. — engine
5. Workload matrix (≥3 prompts incl. chat template, 256 tokens) and n ≥ 3 for arms < 5 % apart. — spec

# Strata over-memory MoE study for Jetson Orin Nano 8 GB (read-only, 2026-11-10)

Strata = campaign/ref/Strata @504b1433 (paths below relative to it). llama.cpp = campaign/ref/llama.cpp @31288c9c6.
Unverified items are marked (U). Nothing was built or run.

## 1. Strata mechanism for models larger than memory

Strata is NOT a generic "stream everything from SSD" engine. It is a 3-tier expert placement: VRAM cache -> RAM (or mmap'd
file pages) -> SSD file tier. Hot experts are on GPU; misses are computed in place by CPU threads in parallel with the GPU.
- Resident on GPU: attention/DeltaNet mixers, routers, shared experts, head, KV (from 64K only its hot part, rest streams
  from RAM), plus an expert cache filling remaining VRAM (docs/HOW_IT_WORKS.md:14-25).
- Resident in RAM: all experts, pinned; CPU computes the non-cached ones "in place" concurrently (HOW_IT_WORKS.md:27-29).
- Over-memory regime (the relevant one): DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 2.00 bpw, 138 GB experts + 111 GB n-gram table. Experts go
  "as many as fit in graphics memory; the rest computed on the CPU, read in place from the model files"; n-gram table stays
  on SSD, a few rows per token (docs/DEEPSEEK41.md:13-17). "With less memory than that, part of the CPU's experts are read
  from the SSD while the model answers. It runs, slowly" (DEEPSEEK41.md:23-25). Measured: RTX5070 12GB + 64GB RAM + 3.6GB/s
  NVMe ~4.7 tok/s (DEEPSEEK41.md:63-65); Strix Halo 128GB unified, 109 GB experts in pool + 23 GB from SSD, 19-21 tok/s code
  (DEEPSEEK41.md:51-55). RAM-capped runs on 1 GPU: 26 tok/s unlimited -> 21/18/15/8 at 40/32/24/16 GB RAM (DEEPSEEK41.md:89-91).
  Planner: uma headroom = MemAvailable - 6 GiB (`DS4_UMA_HEADROOM_GIB`), because page cache of the model files is most of
  what cudaMemGetInfo counted (DGX_SPARK_LINUX.md:84-86).
